TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The L1 column equivalence is the product of the identity and the supplied
non-output coordinate equivalence, followed by `finProdFinEquiv`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem l1ColCoord_eq (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p) :
    S.l1ColCoord kappa p f =
      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.refl _) (S.mCoord kappa p f)).trans finProdFinEquiv

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Garbling coordinates are ordered with output coordinates first, then
non-output coordinates, as in [AGW20, Appendix A, (31), p.38].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def outputCoord (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p) :
    (Fin (n.eval kappa) ⊕ S.MIdx kappa p f) ≃
      Fin (n.eval kappa + S.mCount kappa p f) :=
  (Equiv.sumCongr (Equiv.refl _) (S.mCoord kappa p f)).trans finSumFinEquiv

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The output-coordinate equivalence is the sum of the identity and the
supplied non-output coordinate equivalence, followed by `finSumFinEquiv`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem outputCoord_eq (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p) :
    S.outputCoord kappa p f =
      (Equiv.sumCongr (Equiv.refl _) (S.mCoord kappa p f)).trans finSumFinEquiv

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
A non-output index is encoded by the fixed-width binary numeral of its
supplied finite coordinate. This is representation glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def encMIdx (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p) (u : S.MIdx kappa p f) : List Bool :=
  Candidates.natToList (Nat.size (S.mCount kappa p f)) (S.mCoord kappa p f u).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The non-output index encoding is the numeral of its finite coordinate.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem encMIdx_eq (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p) (u : S.MIdx kappa p f) :
    S.encMIdx kappa p f u =
      Candidates.natToList (Nat.size (S.mCount kappa p f)) (S.mCoord kappa p f u).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
An auxiliary index is encoded by the fixed-width binary numeral of its
supplied finite coordinate. This is representation glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def encTIdx (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p) (u : S.TIdx kappa p f) : List Bool :=
  Candidates.natToList (Nat.size (S.auxCount kappa p f)) (S.tCoord kappa p f u).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The auxiliary index encoding is the numeral of its finite coordinate.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem encTIdx_eq (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p) (u : S.TIdx kappa p f) :
    S.encTIdx kappa p f u =
      Candidates.natToList (Nat.size (S.auxCount kappa p f)) (S.tCoord kappa p f u).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The matrix-generation output is the nested pair of the two row-major matrix
encodings, at the modulus's binary width. Existing modular encodings are reused.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def encLgen (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode
    (Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (Nat.size (p : ℕ))
      (fun i j => S.L1 kappa p f ((S.rowCoord kappa p f).symm i)
        ((S.l1ColCoord kappa p f).symm j)))
    (Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (Nat.size (p : ℕ))
      (fun i j => S.L0 kappa p f ((S.rowCoord kappa p f).symm i)
        ((S.mCoord kappa p f).symm j)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The matrix-generation output is the pair of the displayed modular matrix
encodings, in the supplied canonical coordinate orders.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem encLgen_eq (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p) :
    S.encLgen kappa p f = pairEncode
      (Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (Nat.size (p : ℕ))
        (fun i j => S.L1 kappa p f ((S.rowCoord kappa p f).symm i)
          ((S.l1ColCoord kappa p f).symm j)))
      (Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (Nat.size (p : ℕ))
        (fun i j => S.L0 kappa p f ((S.rowCoord kappa p f).symm i)
          ((S.mCoord kappa p f).symm j)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The reconstruction output is the fixed-width modular vector encoding in the
canonical garbling-coordinate order. Existing modular encodings are reused.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def encRec (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p)
    (x : Fin (l.eval kappa) → ZMod (p : ℕ)) : List Bool :=
  Encoding.Modular.encodeVector (Nat.size (p : ℕ))
    (fun i => S.recVec kappa p f x ((S.outputCoord kappa p f).symm i))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The reconstruction output is the displayed modular vector encoding.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem encRec_eq (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p)
    (x : Fin (l.eval kappa) → ZMod (p : ℕ)) :
    S.encRec kappa p f x = Encoding.Modular.encodeVector (Nat.size (p : ℕ))
      (fun i => S.recVec kappa p f x ((S.outputCoord kappa p f).symm i))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Matrix generation reads the unary security parameter and the pair of public
parameters with the function description. This is uniform input-layout glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def lgenInput (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p) : List Bool :=
  NUPPT.advInput kappa (pairEncode (paramWord l n kappa p) (List.ofFn (S.encFn kappa p f)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The matrix-generation input is the displayed adversary-input layout, with
modulus and dimensions supplied in `paramWord`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem lgenInput_eq (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p) :
    S.lgenInput kappa p f = NUPPT.advInput kappa
      (pairEncode (paramWord l n kappa p) (List.ofFn (S.encFn kappa p f)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Reconstruction reads the security parameter, public parameters, function
and public input. All residues use the positive modulus supplied on the input.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def recInput (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p)
    (x : Fin (l.eval kappa) → ZMod (p : ℕ)) : List Bool :=
  NUPPT.advInput kappa (pairEncode (paramWord l n kappa p)
    (pairEncode (List.ofFn (S.encFn kappa p f))
      (Encoding.Modular.encodeVector (Nat.size (p : ℕ)) x)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The reconstruction input is the displayed nested pair containing the
function description and fixed-width public-input residues.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem recInput_eq (kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p)
    (x : Fin (l.eval kappa) → ZMod (p : ℕ)) :
    S.recInput kappa p f x = NUPPT.advInput kappa (pairEncode (paramWord l n kappa p)
      (pairEncode (List.ofFn (S.encFn kappa p f))
        (Encoding.Modular.encodeVector (Nat.size (p : ℕ)) x)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
A partial-garbling interface includes uniform efficient matrix generation
and reconstruction. [AGW20, Lemma 2, p.12; IW14, Definition 1 continuation, p.7].
One polynomial-time map is chosen before κ and the positive modulus in each
field. The other two algorithms are the canonical matrix formulas, so they
require no independently chosen algorithm or sampler.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
structure PartialGarbling (l n : PolyExpr) (Fn : (kappa : ℕ) → ℕ+ → Type)
    extends PartialGarbling.Raw l n Fn where
  /-- One deterministic polynomial-time map generates both encoded matrices for
  all security parameters, positive moduli and encoded functions. -/
  lgen_eff : ∃ a : List Bool → List Bool, PolyTimeComputable a ∧
    ∀ kappa (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p),
      a (toRaw.lgenInput kappa p f) = toRaw.encLgen kappa p f
  /-- One deterministic polynomial-time map reconstructs the encoded vector for
  all security parameters, positive moduli, functions and public inputs. -/
  rec_eff : ∃ a : List Bool → List Bool, PolyTimeComputable a ∧
    ∀ kappa (p : ℕ+) (f : Fn kappa p) (x : Fin (l.eval kappa) → ZMod (p : ℕ)),
      a (toRaw.recInput kappa p f x) = toRaw.encRec kappa p f x

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The efficient interface's raw family has the same non-output index types.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem toRaw_MIdx : S.toRaw.MIdx = S.MIdx

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The efficient interface's raw family has the same auxiliary index types.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem toRaw_TIdx : S.toRaw.TIdx = S.TIdx

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The efficient interface's raw family has the same coefficient matrices L1.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem toRaw_L1 : S.toRaw.L1 = S.L1

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The efficient interface's raw family has the same constant matrices L0.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem toRaw_L0 : S.toRaw.L0 = S.L0

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The efficient interface's raw family has the same reconstruction vectors.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem toRaw_rec : S.toRaw.recVec = S.recVec

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The efficient interface's raw family has the same evaluated vector functions.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem toRaw_eval : S.toRaw.eval = S.eval

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Non-output nodes are all padded public-variable prefixes of lengths 0 through d.
This is the layered specialization of [AGW20, Appendix A, p.37].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: abbrev MIdx (l d : ℕ) : Type := Σ k : Fin (d + 1), Fin k.val → Fin (l + 1)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Non-output indices have the displayed prefix-node type.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem mIdx_eq (l d : ℕ) :
    MIdx l d = (Σ k : Fin (d + 1), Fin k.val → Fin (l + 1))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Auxiliary draw nodes are all non-root prefixes, indexed by their predecessor
length. [AGW20, Appendix A, (28)–(32), pp.37–38], layered specialization.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: abbrev TIdx (l d : ℕ) : Type := Σ k : Fin d, Fin (k.val + 1) → Fin (l + 1)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Auxiliary draw indices have the displayed non-root-prefix type.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem tIdx_eq (l d : ℕ) :
    TIdx l d = (Σ k : Fin d, Fin (k.val + 1) → Fin (l + 1))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The distinguished coordinate is the empty prefix, namely the source node.
[AGW20, Appendix A, (30), p.37].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: def root (l d : ℕ) : MIdx l d := ⟨⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_succ d⟩, Fin.elim0⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The distinguished coordinate is the explicit depth-zero prefix.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem root_eq (l d : ℕ) : root l d = ⟨⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_succ d⟩, Fin.elim0⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: An auxiliary prefix is viewed as its corresponding non-output node.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: def node {l d : ℕ} (v : TIdx l d) : MIdx l d := ⟨v.1.succ, v.2⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The auxiliary-node embedding increments its predecessor depth.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem node_eq {l d : ℕ} (v : TIdx l d) : node v = ⟨v.1.succ, v.2⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The parent of a non-root prefix deletes its last label.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: def parent {l d : ℕ} (v : TIdx l d) : MIdx l d := ⟨v.1.castSucc, Fin.init v.2⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The parent is the prefix obtained by the published tuple-init operation.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem parent_eq {l d : ℕ} (v : TIdx l d) :
    parent v = ⟨v.1.castSucc, Fin.init v.2⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The edge into a non-root prefix is labeled by its final tuple coordinate.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: def lastLabel {l d : ℕ} (v : TIdx l d) : Fin (l + 1) := v.2 (Fin.last v.1.val)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The final edge label is the prefix's last coordinate.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem lastLabel_eq {l d : ℕ} (v : TIdx l d) :
    lastLabel v = v.2 (Fin.last v.1.val)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A full public-variable tuple identifies its depth-d terminal prefix.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: def leaf {l d : ℕ} (tau : Fin d → Fin (l + 1)) : MIdx l d := ⟨Fin.last d, tau⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A leaf has depth d and the supplied tuple.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem leaf_eq {l d : ℕ} (tau : Fin d → Fin (l + 1)) :
    leaf tau = ⟨Fin.last d, tau⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The number of non-output nodes is the sum of padded-prefix counts at every
level. This depends only on l,d, not on coefficients.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: def nodeCount (l d : ℕ) : ℕ := ∑ k : Fin (d + 1), (l + 1) ^ k.val

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The non-output node count is the displayed geometric sum.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem nodeCount_eq (l d : ℕ) : nodeCount l d = ∑ k : Fin (d + 1), (l + 1) ^ k.val

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The number of auxiliary coordinates is the sum of positive-depth prefix counts.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: def auxCount (l d : ℕ) : ℕ := ∑ k : Fin d, (l + 1) ^ (k.val + 1)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The auxiliary coordinate count is the displayed positive-depth sum.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem auxCount_eq (l d : ℕ) : auxCount l d = ∑ k : Fin d, (l + 1) ^ (k.val + 1)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The fixed node bound is the polynomial sum of (l+1)^k for 0≤k≤d.
It is independent of the modulus and function coefficients. [AGW20, Lemma 2,
p.12], specialized to the fixed-degree layered representation.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def nodeBound (l : PolyExpr) : ℕ → PolyExpr
  | 0 => .const 1
  | d + 1 => .add (nodeBound l d) (.pow (.add l (PolyExpr.const 1)) (d + 1))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: At degree zero the node bound is the constant polynomial 1.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem nodeBound_zero (l : PolyExpr) : nodeBound l 0 = .const 1

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Increasing the degree adds the count of the next prefix layer.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem nodeBound_succ (l : PolyExpr) (d : ℕ) :
    nodeBound l (d + 1) = .add (nodeBound l d) (.pow (.add l (PolyExpr.const 1)) (d + 1))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The polynomial node bound equals the exact geometric node count.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem nodeBound_eval (l : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) :
    (nodeBound l d).eval kappa = nodeCount (l.eval kappa) d

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Removing the source leaves exactly the auxiliary prefix nodes.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem auxCount_add_one (l d : ℕ) : auxCount l d + 1 = nodeCount l d

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Node coordinates use the explicit tuple equivalence within each depth and
the published finite-sigma equivalence between depths. No opaque enumeration is used.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def nodeCoord (l d : ℕ) : MIdx l d ≃ Fin (nodeCount l d) :=
  (Equiv.sigmaCongrRight (fun k : Fin (d + 1) => tupleCoord l k.val)).trans finSigmaFinEquiv

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Node coordinates are the displayed composition of public equivalences.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem nodeCoord_eq (l d : ℕ) : nodeCoord l d =
    (Equiv.sigmaCongrRight (fun k : Fin (d + 1) => tupleCoord l k.val)).trans
      finSigmaFinEquiv

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Auxiliary coordinates use explicit positive-depth tuple ranks and finite-sigma ranks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def auxCoord (l d : ℕ) : TIdx l d ≃ Fin (auxCount l d) :=
  (Equiv.sigmaCongrRight (fun k : Fin d => tupleCoord l (k.val + 1))).trans finSigmaFinEquiv

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Auxiliary coordinates are the displayed composition of public equivalences.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem auxCoord_eq (l d : ℕ) : auxCoord l d =
    (Equiv.sigmaCongrRight (fun k : Fin d => tupleCoord l (k.val + 1))).trans
      finSigmaFinEquiv

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The source is finite coordinate zero, fixing the distinguished e1 position.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem nodeCoord_root (l d : ℕ) : (nodeCoord l d (root l d)).val = 0

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
L1 places the variable-edge coefficients at parent columns and child rows.
Output rows are zero. This is the layered coefficient matrix of
[AGW20, Appendix A, (32), p.38], with the corrected t×(lm) shape.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def L1 (C : PolyTensor p l n d) :
    Matrix (TIdx l d ⊕ Fin n) (Fin l × MIdx l d) (ZMod (p : ℕ)) :=
  fun row iu => match row with
    | Sum.inl v => if iu.2 = parent v ∧ lastLabel v = iu.1.castSucc then 1 else 0
    | Sum.inr _ => 0

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A non-root L1 row records the variable-labeled edge from its parent.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem L1_inl (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (v : TIdx l d) (i : Fin l) (u : MIdx l d) :
    L1 C (Sum.inl v) (i, u) =
      if u = parent v ∧ lastLabel v = i.castSucc then 1 else 0

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Every output row of L1 is zero.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem L1_inr (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (j : Fin n) (iu : Fin l × MIdx l d) :
    L1 C (Sum.inr j) iu = 0

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
L0 records constant-labeled edges, the negative non-root diagonal, and the
terminal coefficient edges. [AGW20, Appendix A, (32), p.38], layered specialization.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def L0 (C : PolyTensor p l n d) :
    Matrix (TIdx l d ⊕ Fin n) (MIdx l d) (ZMod (p : ℕ)) :=
  fun row u => match row with
    | Sum.inl v =>
      (if u = parent v ∧ lastLabel v = Fin.last l then 1 else 0) -
        (if u = node v then 1 else 0)
    | Sum.inr j => ∑ tau : Fin d → Fin (l + 1), if u = leaf tau then C j tau else 0

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A non-root L0 row contains its constant edge and negative diagonal.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem L0_inl (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (v : TIdx l d) (u : MIdx l d) :
    L0 C (Sum.inl v) u =
      (if u = parent v ∧ lastLabel v = Fin.last l then 1 else 0) -
        (if u = node v then 1 else 0)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: An output L0 row contains precisely the corresponding terminal coefficients.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem L0_inr (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (j : Fin n) (u : MIdx l d) :
    L0 C (Sum.inr j) u =
      ∑ tau : Fin d → Fin (l + 1), if u = leaf tau then C j tau else 0

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The public-input matrix combines the variable and constant parts as in
[AGW20, Appendix A, (32), p.38].
The input matrix is exactly L1(x⊗I)+L0.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem matrix_eq (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ)) :
    matrix C x = L1 C * PartialGarbling.publicTensor x + L0 C

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
A forward path value is the product of the labels in its prefix. This replaces
the cofactor description of rec in [AGW20, Appendix A, p.38] by its path formula.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def forward (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ)) (u : MIdx l d) : ZMod (p : ℕ) :=
  ∏ i : Fin u.1.val, xhat x (u.2 i)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Forward values are the displayed finite label products.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem forward_eq (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ)) (u : MIdx l d) :
    forward x u = ∏ i : Fin u.1.val, xhat x (u.2 i)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The source's forward value is the empty product 1.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem forward_root (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ)) : forward x (root l d) = 1

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Reconstruction consists of the polynomial outputs followed by all forward
prefix values. [AGW20, Lemma 2, p.12; Appendix A, p.38].
The output-coordinate reconstruction block is the evaluated polynomial vector.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem rec_inl (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ)) (j : Fin n) :
    rec C x (Sum.inl j) = polyTensorEval C x j

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The non-output reconstruction block is the forward prefix vector.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem rec_inr (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ)) (u : MIdx l d) :
    rec C x (Sum.inr u) = forward x u

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Extend a prefix by a suffix to obtain a full degree-d tuple. The length cast
uses the prefix's certified bound and does not choose an enumeration.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def extend (u : MIdx l d) (sigma : Fin (d - u.1.val) → Fin (l + 1)) :
    Fin d → Fin (l + 1) :=
  fun i => Fin.append u.2 sigma
    (Fin.cast (Nat.add_sub_of_le (Nat.le_of_lt_succ u.1.isLt)).symm i)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Prefix extension is the displayed tuple append after the canonical length cast.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem extend_eq (u : MIdx l d) (sigma : Fin (d - u.1.val) → Fin (l + 1)) :
    extend u sigma = fun i => Fin.append u.2 sigma
      (Fin.cast (Nat.add_sub_of_le (Nat.le_of_lt_succ u.1.isLt)).symm i)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
A backward value sums all suffix paths, weighted by terminal coefficients and
private values. This is the path form of the source's privacy translation.
[AGW20, Appendix A, (28)–(30), p.37; IW14, §4.2, p.11].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def backward (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ))
    (z : Fin n → ZMod (p : ℕ)) (u : MIdx l d) : ZMod (p : ℕ) :=
  ∑ sigma : Fin (d - u.1.val) → Fin (l + 1),
    (∑ j : Fin n, C j (extend u sigma) * z j) *
      ∏ i : Fin (d - u.1.val), xhat x (sigma i)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Backward values are the displayed finite suffix sums.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem backward_eq (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ))
    (z : Fin n → ZMod (p : ℕ)) (u : MIdx l d) :
    backward C x z u =
      ∑ sigma : Fin (d - u.1.val) → Fin (l + 1),
        (∑ j : Fin n, C j (extend u sigma) * z j) *
          ∏ i : Fin (d - u.1.val), xhat x (sigma i)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The draw translation uses backward values at non-root nodes and the private
values at output nodes. [AGW20, Appendix A, (28)–(30), p.37], path-sum proof route.
The auxiliary draw shift is the corresponding node's backward value.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem shift_inl (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ))
    (z : Fin n → ZMod (p : ℕ)) (v : TIdx l d) :
    shift C x z (Sum.inl v) = backward C x z (node v)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The output draw shift equals the original private vector.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem shift_inr (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ))
    (z : Fin n → ZMod (p : ℕ)) (j : Fin n) : shift C x z (Sum.inr j) = z j

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Applying the input matrix to forward values cancels every internal prefix
row and leaves exactly the polynomial vector on output rows.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem forward_action (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ)) :
    Matrix.mulVec (matrix C x) (forward x) =
      Sum.elim (fun _ : TIdx l d => 0) (polyTensorEval C x)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The backward value at the source is the allowed scalar z·f(x).
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem backward_root (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ))
    (z : Fin n → ZMod (p : ℕ)) :
    backward C x z (root l d) = dotProduct z (polyTensorEval C x)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Multiplying the backward draw shift by the input matrix cancels every column
except the source column, whose value is the allowed scalar.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem backward_action (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ))
    (z : Fin n → ZMod (p : ℕ)) :
    Matrix.vecMul (shift C x z) (matrix C x) =
      fun u => if u = root l d then dotProduct z (polyTensorEval C x) else 0

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Every real garbling reconstructs z·f(x), independently of its draw.
[AGW20, Lemma 2, p.12; Appendix A, p.38], proved by path sums.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem rec_spec (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ))
    (z : Fin n → ZMod (p : ℕ)) (t : (TIdx l d ⊕ Fin n) → ZMod (p : ℕ)) :
    dotProduct (PartialGarbling.pgbCore (L1 C) (L0 C) x z t) (rec C x) =
      dotProduct z (polyTensorEval C x)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Subtracting the backward draw shift transforms the real garbling exactly
into the simulated garbling at its allowed scalar. [AGW20, Appendix A, (28)–(30),
p.37; IW14, §4.2, p.11], with path sums replacing the determinant argument.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem translation (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ))
    (z : Fin n → ZMod (p : ℕ)) (t : (TIdx l d ⊕ Fin n) → ZMod (p : ℕ)) :
    PartialGarbling.pgbCore (L1 C) (L0 C) x z t =
      PartialGarbling.pgbStarCore (L1 C) (L0 C) (root l d) x
        (dotProduct z (polyTensorEval C x)) (t - shift C x z)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Real and simulated layered garblings have identical laws, with no error term.
[IW14, Definition 1, p.6; AGW20, Appendix A, (28)–(30), p.37].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem privacy (C : PolyTensor p l n d) (x : Fin l → ZMod (p : ℕ))
    (z : Fin n → ZMod (p : ℕ)) (test : ((Fin n ⊕ MIdx l d) → ZMod (p : ℕ)) → ℝ) :
    ProbComp.expect (ProbComp.sample ((TIdx l d ⊕ Fin n) → ZMod (p : ℕ)))
        (fun t => test (PartialGarbling.pgbCore (L1 C) (L0 C) x z t)) =
      ProbComp.expect (ProbComp.sample ((TIdx l d ⊕ Fin n) → ZMod (p : ℕ)))
        (fun t => test (PartialGarbling.pgbStarCore (L1 C) (L0 C) (root l d)
          x (dotProduct z (polyTensorEval C x)) t))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The layered raw family instantiates the corrected partial-garbling interface
for padded polynomial tensors. [AGW20, Appendix A, (28)–(32), pp.37–38; IW14,
Theorem 3, p.8], specialized to one private-tail column.

The algorithms and index coordinates are explicit. Correctness and exact privacy
use forward/backward path sums and translation, rather than determinants. The
family covers every positive modulus; no efficiency proof is assumed or constructed.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def layeredPG_raw (l n : PolyExpr) (d : ℕ) :
    PartialGarbling.Raw l n (fun kappa p => PolyTensor p (l.eval kappa) (n.eval kappa) d) where
  MIdx := fun kappa _ _ => PartialGarbling.Layered.MIdx (l.eval kappa) d
  TIdx := fun kappa _ _ => PartialGarbling.Layered.TIdx (l.eval kappa) d
  mFinite := fun _ _ _ => inferInstance
  tFinite := fun _ _ _ => inferInstance
  mDecEq := fun _ _ _ => inferInstance
  tDecEq := fun _ _ _ => inferInstance
  mCount := fun kappa _ _ => PartialGarbling.Layered.nodeCount (l.eval kappa) d
  mBound := PartialGarbling.Layered.nodeBound l d
  mCount_le_mBound := fun kappa _ _ =>
    (PartialGarbling.Layered.nodeBound_eval l d kappa).ge
  auxCount := fun kappa _ _ => PartialGarbling.Layered.auxCount (l.eval kappa) d
  mCoord := fun kappa _ _ => PartialGarbling.Layered.nodeCoord (l.eval kappa) d
  tCoord := fun kappa _ _ => PartialGarbling.Layered.auxCoord (l.eval kappa) d
  auxCount_add_one := fun kappa _ _ =>
    PartialGarbling.Layered.auxCount_add_one (l.eval kappa) d
  m0 := fun kappa _ _ => PartialGarbling.Layered.root (l.eval kappa) d
  m0_coord := fun kappa _ _ => PartialGarbling.Layered.nodeCoord_root (l.eval kappa) d
  fnLen := fun kappa p => n.eval kappa * (l.eval kappa + 1) ^ d * Nat.size (p : ℕ)
  encFn := fun _ p C => encodeTensorBits (Nat.size (p : ℕ)) C
  encFn_inj := fun _ p => encodeTensorBits_injective (Nat.size (p : ℕ))
    (Nat.le_of_lt (Nat.lt_size_self (p : ℕ)))
  eval := fun _ _ C => polyTensorEval C
  L1 := fun _ _ C => PartialGarbling.Layered.L1 C
  L0 := fun _ _ C => PartialGarbling.Layered.L0 C
  recVec := fun _ _ C => PartialGarbling.Layered.rec C
  rec_spec := fun _ _ C => PartialGarbling.Layered.rec_spec C
  privacy := fun _ _ C => PartialGarbling.Layered.privacy C

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The layered raw family's non-output coordinates are exactly its prefix nodes.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_MIdx (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+)
    (C : PolyTensor p (l.eval kappa) (n.eval kappa) d) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).MIdx kappa p C =
      PartialGarbling.Layered.MIdx (l.eval kappa) d

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The layered raw family's auxiliary coordinates are exactly its non-root prefixes.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_TIdx (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+)
    (C : PolyTensor p (l.eval kappa) (n.eval kappa) d) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).TIdx kappa p C =
      PartialGarbling.Layered.TIdx (l.eval kappa) d

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The layered non-output dimension is independent of the coefficient tensor.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_mCount (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+)
    (C : PolyTensor p (l.eval kappa) (n.eval kappa) d) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).mCount kappa p C =
      PartialGarbling.Layered.nodeCount (l.eval kappa) d

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The raw family's fixed bound is the polynomial sum of its layer counts.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_mBound (l n : PolyExpr) (d : ℕ) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).mBound = PartialGarbling.Layered.nodeBound l d

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The bound evaluates to the exact node count, so padded reductions lose no
extra statistical term from the layered instance's dimension bound.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_mBound_eval (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).mBound.eval kappa =
      PartialGarbling.Layered.nodeCount (l.eval kappa) d

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The layered auxiliary dimension is independent of the coefficient tensor.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_auxCount (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+)
    (C : PolyTensor p (l.eval kappa) (n.eval kappa) d) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).auxCount kappa p C =
      PartialGarbling.Layered.auxCount (l.eval kappa) d

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The raw matrix-generation algorithms are the explicit layered matrices L1.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_L1 (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+)
    (C : PolyTensor p (l.eval kappa) (n.eval kappa) d) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).L1 kappa p C = PartialGarbling.Layered.L1 C

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The raw constant matrices are the explicit layered matrices L0.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_L0 (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+)
    (C : PolyTensor p (l.eval kappa) (n.eval kappa) d) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).L0 kappa p C = PartialGarbling.Layered.L0 C

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The raw reconstruction algorithm is the explicit forward path vector.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_rec (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+)
    (C : PolyTensor p (l.eval kappa) (n.eval kappa) d) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).recVec kappa p C = PartialGarbling.Layered.rec C

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The raw evaluated vector is the shared coefficient-tensor evaluation.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_eval (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+)
    (C : PolyTensor p (l.eval kappa) (n.eval kappa) d) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).eval kappa p C = polyTensorEval C

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The raw function-description width follows the input modulus, permitting one
uniform efficient interface for every positive modulus.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_fnLen (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).fnLen kappa p =
      n.eval kappa * (l.eval kappa + 1) ^ d * Nat.size (p : ℕ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The raw function encoding is the shared canonical tensor encoding.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_encFn (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+)
    (C : PolyTensor p (l.eval kappa) (n.eval kappa) d) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).encFn kappa p C = encodeTensorBits (Nat.size (p : ℕ)) C

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The raw distinguished coordinate is the empty prefix.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_m0 (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+)
    (C : PolyTensor p (l.eval kappa) (n.eval kappa) d) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).m0 kappa p C = PartialGarbling.Layered.root (l.eval kappa) d

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The raw non-output coordinate encoding uses explicit tuple and depth ranks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_mCoord (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+)
    (C : PolyTensor p (l.eval kappa) (n.eval kappa) d) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).mCoord kappa p C =
      PartialGarbling.Layered.nodeCoord (l.eval kappa) d

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The raw auxiliary coordinate encoding uses explicit positive-depth tuple ranks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_raw_tCoord (l n : PolyExpr) (d kappa : ℕ) (p : ℕ+)
    (C : PolyTensor p (l.eval kappa) (n.eval kappa) d) :
    (layeredPG_raw l n d).tCoord kappa p C =
      PartialGarbling.Layered.auxCoord (l.eval kappa) d

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
A deterministic answer function is an oracle implementation that returns its answer and
next state with no calls to the target oracles. Technical glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def detImpl (h : ∀ i, spec.dom i → σ → spec.rng i × σ) : QueryImpl spec σ spec' :=
  fun i x s => .pure (h i x s)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The deterministic implementation answers `i, x` from state `s` by returning `h i x s`:
`detImpl h i x s = pure (h i x s)`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem detImpl_apply (h : ∀ i, spec.dom i → σ → spec.rng i × σ)
    (i : ι) (x : spec.dom i) (s : σ) :
    detImpl (spec' := spec') h i x s = .pure (h i x s)

def runDet (next : QueryLog spec → Move spec α) (timeout : α)
    (h : ∀ i, spec.dom i → σ → spec.rng i × σ) :
    ℕ → QueryLog spec → σ → α × σ
  | 0, hist, s => match next hist with
    | .ret a => (a, s)
    | .query _ _ => (timeout, s)
  | q + 1, hist, s => match next hist with
    | .ret a => (a, s)
    | .query i x =>
      let ys := h i x s
      runDet next timeout h q (hist ++ [⟨i, x, ys.1⟩]) ys.2

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: With no query budget, a final output `a` is returned with the state unchanged.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem runDet_zero_of_ret {a : α} (hn : next hist = .ret a) :
    runDet next timeout h 0 hist s = (a, s)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: With no query budget, a query returns `timeout` with the state unchanged.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem runDet_zero_of_query {i : ι} {x : spec.dom i} (hn : next hist = .query i x) :
    runDet next timeout h 0 hist s = (timeout, s)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: With positive query budget, a final output `a` is returned with the state unchanged.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem runDet_succ_of_ret {q : ℕ} {a : α} (hn : next hist = .ret a) :
    runDet next timeout h (q + 1) hist s = (a, s)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
With positive query budget, a query consumes one unit, extends the history by its answer,
and continues from the next state supplied by `h`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem runDet_succ_of_query {q : ℕ} {i : ι} {x : spec.dom i}
    (hn : next hist = .query i x) :
    runDet next timeout h (q + 1) hist s =
      runDet next timeout h q (hist ++ [⟨i, x, (h i x s).1⟩]) (h i x s).2

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Simulating a bounded next-move computation with deterministic stateful answers returns the
point mass at its deterministic output and final state. This is the simulation equation used
to relate deterministic reductions to handler realisers. Technical glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem simulate_buildComp_detImpl_eq_pure
    (next : QueryLog spec → Move spec α) (timeout : α)
    (h : ∀ i, spec.dom i → σ → spec.rng i × σ)
    (q : ℕ) (hist : QueryLog spec) (s : σ) :
    simulate (detImpl (spec' := spec') h) (buildComp next timeout q hist) s =
      .pure (runDet next timeout h q hist s)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Challenge queries contain the public and private words; key queries contain
one function description. [Wee20, §2.2, p.5].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
abbrev saIn (S : FEScheme.Raw C) (kappa : ℕ) : Fin 2 → ℕ
  | 0 => C.pubLen.eval kappa + C.privLen.eval kappa
  | 1 => C.fnLen.eval kappa

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The challenge-query width is the sum of the input widths.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saIn_zero (kappa : ℕ) :
    S.saIn kappa 0 = C.pubLen.eval kappa + C.privLen.eval kappa

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The key-query width is the function-description width.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem saIn_one (kappa : ℕ) : S.saIn kappa 1 = C.fnLen.eval kappa

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Oracle answers contain one validity bit and a ciphertext or key encoding.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
abbrev saOut (kappa : ℕ) : Fin 2 → ℕ
  | 0 => S.ctLen.eval kappa + 1
  | 1 => S.skLen.eval kappa + 1

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The challenge answer has one validity bit and its ciphertext payload.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem saOut_zero (kappa : ℕ) : S.saOut kappa 0 = S.ctLen.eval kappa + 1

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The key answer has one validity bit and its key payload.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem saOut_one (kappa : ℕ) : S.saOut kappa 1 = S.skLen.eval kappa + 1

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The semi-adaptive specification is the library's fixed-width bit specification.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: abbrev saSpec (kappa : ℕ) : OracleSpec (Fin 2) := bitSpec (S.saIn kappa) (S.saOut kappa)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The oracle specification has exactly the displayed input and output widths.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saSpec_eq (kappa : ℕ) :
    S.saSpec kappa = bitSpec (S.saIn kappa) (S.saOut kappa)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The machine codec is the library's bitCodec with a one-bit final output.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def saCodec (kappa : ℕ) : MachineCodec (S.saSpec kappa) (Fin 1 → Bool) :=
  bitCodec (S.saIn kappa) (S.saOut kappa) 1

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The semi-adaptive codec is the displayed instance of bitCodec.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saCodec_eq (kappa : ℕ) :
    S.saCodec kappa = bitCodec (S.saIn kappa) (S.saOut kappa) 1

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Combine the typed public/private challenge words into one oracle query.
Challenge queries append the private word to the public word.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saChallengeQuery_eq (kappa : ℕ) (x : Fin (C.pubLen.eval kappa) → Bool)
    (y : Fin (C.privLen.eval kappa) → Bool) :
    S.saChallengeQuery kappa x y = Fin.append x y

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Split a challenge query into its typed public and private input words.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def saSplitChallenge (kappa : ℕ) (xy : (S.saSpec kappa).dom 0) :
    (Fin (C.pubLen.eval kappa) → Bool) × (Fin (C.privLen.eval kappa) → Bool) :=
  (fun i => xy (Fin.castAdd (C.privLen.eval kappa) i),
    fun j => xy (Fin.natAdd (C.pubLen.eval kappa) j))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The challenge's public word occupies its first input block.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saSplitChallenge_fst (kappa : ℕ) (xy : (S.saSpec kappa).dom 0) :
    (S.saSplitChallenge kappa xy).1 =
      fun i => xy (Fin.castAdd (C.privLen.eval kappa) i)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The challenge's private word occupies its second input block.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saSplitChallenge_snd (kappa : ℕ) (xy : (S.saSpec kappa).dom 0) :
    (S.saSplitChallenge kappa xy).2 =
      fun j => xy (Fin.natAdd (C.pubLen.eval kappa) j)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Read the typed function description from a key query.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def saKeyFunction (kappa : ℕ) (f : (S.saSpec kappa).dom 1) :
    Fin (C.fnLen.eval kappa) → Bool := f

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The key query is already the function-description word.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saKeyFunction_eq (kappa : ℕ) (f : (S.saSpec kappa).dom 1) :
    S.saKeyFunction kappa f = f

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A typed challenge request is a query to oracle zero.
The challenge move has the displayed oracle and combined query.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saChallengeMove_eq (kappa : ℕ) (x : Fin (C.pubLen.eval kappa) → Bool)
    (y : Fin (C.privLen.eval kappa) → Bool) :
    S.saChallengeMove kappa x y = .query 0 (S.saChallengeQuery kappa x y)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A typed key request is a query to oracle one.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def saKeyMove (kappa : ℕ) (f : Fin (C.fnLen.eval kappa) → Bool) :
    Move (S.saSpec kappa) Bool := .query 1 f

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The key move has the displayed oracle and function description.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saKeyMove_eq (kappa : ℕ) (f : Fin (C.fnLen.eval kappa) → Bool) :
    S.saKeyMove kappa f = .query 1 f

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode an optional typed ciphertext using the common validity-bit answer format.
Ciphertext answers use decAnswer on the optional ciphertext encoding.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saCTAnswer_eq (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (ct : Option (S.CT kappa pp)) : S.saCTAnswer kappa pp ct =
    TCSlib.Cryptography.Composability.FixedLengthScheme.decAnswer (ct.map (S.encCT kappa pp))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode an optional typed key using the common validity-bit answer format.
Key answers use decAnswer on the optional key encoding.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saSKAnswer_eq (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (sk : Option (S.SK kappa pp)) : S.saSKAnswer kappa pp sk =
    TCSlib.Cryptography.Composability.FixedLengthScheme.decAnswer (sk.map (S.encSK kappa pp))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Extract a challenge payload from a successful challenge answer, without
inverting its typed ciphertext encoding. Other oracle answers give none.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def saCTPayload (kappa : ℕ) :
    (i : Fin 2) → (S.saSpec kappa).rng i → Option (Fin (S.ctLen.eval kappa) → Bool)
  | 0, a =>
    let v : Fin (S.ctLen.eval kappa + 1) → Bool := a
    if v 0 then some (Fin.tail v) else none
  | 1, _ => none

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A challenge payload is present exactly when its validity bit is true.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saCTPayload_zero (kappa : ℕ) (a : Fin (S.ctLen.eval kappa + 1) → Bool) :
    S.saCTPayload kappa 0 a = if a 0 then some (Fin.tail a) else none

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A key answer never supplies a challenge payload.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saCTPayload_one (kappa : ℕ) (a : (S.saSpec kappa).rng 1) :
    S.saCTPayload kappa 1 a = none

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Extract a key payload from a successful key answer without recovering a typed
key. Challenge answers give none. This is wire-reading glue for two-stage adversaries.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def saSKPayload (kappa : ℕ) :
    (i : Fin 2) → (S.saSpec kappa).rng i → Option (Fin (S.skLen.eval kappa) → Bool)
  | 0, _ => none
  | 1, a =>
    let v : Fin (S.skLen.eval kappa + 1) → Bool := a
    if v 0 then some (Fin.tail v) else none

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A challenge answer never supplies a key payload.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saSKPayload_zero (kappa : ℕ) (a : (S.saSpec kappa).rng 0) :
    S.saSKPayload kappa 0 a = none

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A key payload is present exactly when its validity bit is true.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saSKPayload_one (kappa : ℕ) (a : Fin (S.skLen.eval kappa + 1) → Bool) :
    S.saSKPayload kappa 1 a = if a 0 then some (Fin.tail a) else none

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The initial adversary word contains public parameters and the master public key.
[Wee20, §2.2, p.5].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def saInputWord (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) (pk : S.MPK kappa pp) :
    List Bool := pairEncode pp.encode (List.ofFn (S.encMPK kappa pp pk))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The adversary's initial word is the displayed pair.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saInputWord_eq (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) (pk : S.MPK kappa pp) :
    S.saInputWord kappa pp pk = pairEncode pp.encode (List.ofFn (S.encMPK kappa pp pk))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
A typed semi-adaptive adversary has one coin polynomial, a total query budget,
and a next move depending on its initial public view, fixed coins and full history.
[Wee20, §2.2, p.5]. Its run is derived by the bounded library interpreter.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
structure SAAdv where
  /-- The number of independent fair coins. -/
  coins : PolyExpr
  /-- The total number of oracle calls allowed, including the challenge. -/
  budget : PolyExpr
  /-- The next move for any public view, coin word and oracle history. -/
  next : (kappa : ℕ) → (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) → S.MPK kappa pp → List Bool →
    QueryLog (S.saSpec kappa) → Move (S.saSpec kappa) Bool

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Run the next-move adversary with its total query budget, timing out to false.
Adversary run is precisely the existing bounded buildComp interpreter.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem run_eq (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) (pk : S.MPK kappa pp)
    (r : List Bool) : A.run kappa pp pk r =
    buildComp (A.next kappa pp pk r) false (A.budget.eval kappa) []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The derived adversary computation never exceeds its total call budget.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem run_costBoundedBy (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (pk : S.MPK kappa pp) (r : List Bool) :
    (A.run kappa pp pk r).CostBoundedBy (fun _ => 1) (A.budget.eval kappa)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A one-bit codec move is read as a Boolean verdict without changing any query.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def saReadMove (kappa : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : Move (S.saSpec kappa) Bool :=
  match (S.saCodec kappa).decodeMove w with
  | .ret b => .ret (b 0)
  | .query i x => .query i x

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The move reader changes only the final one-bit output into Bool.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saReadMove_eq (kappa : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : S.saReadMove kappa w =
    match (S.saCodec kappa).decodeMove w with
    | .ret b => .ret (b 0)
    | .query i x => .query i x

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
An oracle NUPPT uses the standard bitCodec and its encoded initial public view.
[Wee20, §2.2, p.5], instantiated by the library's oracle-machine convention.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def toSAAdv {C : FnClass} {S : FEScheme.Raw C}
    (A : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) : S.SAAdv where
  coins := A.coins
  budget := q
  next := fun kappa pp pk r hist => S.saReadMove kappa
    (A.runAtL kappa (pairEncode (S.saInputWord kappa pp pk)
      ((S.saCodec kappa).encodeLog hist)) r)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The oracle-machine adversary uses its machine's original coin polynomial.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSAAdv_coins {C : FnClass} {S : FEScheme.Raw C}
    (A : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) : (toSAAdv (S := S) A q).coins = A.coins

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The oracle-machine adversary's budget is q total oracle calls.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSAAdv_budget {C : FnClass} {S : FEScheme.Raw C}
    (A : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) : (toSAAdv (S := S) A q).budget = q

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Each next move is one machine activation on its initial view and encoded log.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSAAdv_next {C : FnClass} {S : FEScheme.Raw C}
    (A : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (pk : S.MPK kappa pp) (r : List Bool) (hist : QueryLog (S.saSpec kappa)) :
    (toSAAdv (S := S) A q).next kappa pp pk r hist = S.saReadMove kappa
      (A.runAtL kappa (pairEncode (S.saInputWord kappa pp pk)
        ((S.saCodec kappa).encodeLog hist)) r)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The typed run is exactly toCompOn with bitCodec, followed by reading its one bit.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSAAdv_run {C : FnClass} {S : FEScheme.Raw C}
    (A : NUPPT) (q : PolyExpr) (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (pk : S.MPK kappa pp) (r : A.Coins kappa) :
    (toSAAdv (S := S) A q).run kappa pp pk (List.ofFn r) =
      (fun b => b 0) <$> A.toCompOn
        (bitCodec (S.saIn kappa) (S.saOut kappa) 1)
        kappa (q.eval kappa) (S.saInputWord kappa pp pk) r

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
A semi-adaptive raw simulator yields the committed raw simulator by passing
only omega.publicInput to encryption and the indexed function/scalar to key simulation.
[GJLS21, Definition 4.3; Wee20, §2.2, p.5]. Draws remain the same single draw types.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def toSim : FEScheme.Raw.Simulator.Raw S where
  St := Sim.St
  encSt := Sim.encSt
  encSt_injective := Sim.encSt_injective
  SetupDraw := Sim.SetupDraw
  setupFinite := Sim.setupFinite
  setupNonempty := Sim.setupNonempty
  setupCore := Sim.setupCore
  EncDraw := fun kappa pp st omega => Sim.EncDraw kappa pp st omega.publicInput
  encFinite := fun kappa pp st omega => Sim.encFinite kappa pp st omega.publicInput
  encNonempty := fun kappa pp st omega => Sim.encNonempty kappa pp st omega.publicInput
  encCore := fun kappa pp st omega => Sim.encCore kappa pp st omega.publicInput
  KeyDraw := fun kappa pp st omega j =>
    Sim.KeyDraw kappa pp st omega.publicInput (omega.functions j) (omega.values j)
  keyFinite := fun kappa pp st omega j =>
    Sim.keyFinite kappa pp st omega.publicInput (omega.functions j) (omega.values j)
  keyNonempty := fun kappa pp st omega j =>
    Sim.keyNonempty kappa pp st omega.publicInput (omega.functions j) (omega.values j)
  keyCore := fun kappa pp st omega j =>
    Sim.keyCore kappa pp st omega.publicInput (omega.functions j) (omega.values j)
  encSetupDraw := Sim.encSetupDraw
  encEncDraw := fun kappa pp st omega => Sim.encEncDraw kappa pp st omega.publicInput
  encKeyDraw := fun kappa pp st omega j =>
    Sim.encKeyDraw kappa pp st omega.publicInput (omega.functions j) (omega.values j)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The converted simulator retains the same state family.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem toSim_St : Sim.toSim.St = Sim.St

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The converted simulator retains the same canonical state encoding.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem toSim_encSt : Sim.toSim.encSt = Sim.encSt

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The converted simulator retains the complete setup draw family.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem toSim_SetupDraw : Sim.toSim.SetupDraw = Sim.SetupDraw

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The converted simulator retains the original deterministic setup core.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem toSim_setupCore : Sim.toSim.setupCore = Sim.setupCore

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The converted ciphertext draw depends only on the allowed public input.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSim_EncDraw (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (st : Sim.St kappa pp) (omega : S.Omega kappa pp) :
    Sim.toSim.EncDraw kappa pp st omega = Sim.EncDraw kappa pp st omega.publicInput

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The converted ciphertext core passes only the public input to the raw simulator.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSim_encCore (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (st : Sim.St kappa pp) (omega : S.Omega kappa pp) :
    Sim.toSim.encCore kappa pp st omega = Sim.encCore kappa pp st omega.publicInput

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The converted key draw uses the indexed function and scalar value.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSim_KeyDraw (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (st : Sim.St kappa pp) (omega : S.Omega kappa pp) (j : Fin omega.count) :
    Sim.toSim.KeyDraw kappa pp st omega j =
      Sim.KeyDraw kappa pp st omega.publicInput (omega.functions j) (omega.values j)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The converted key core uses the indexed function and scalar value.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSim_keyCore (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (st : Sim.St kappa pp) (omega : S.Omega kappa pp) (j : Fin omega.count) :
    Sim.toSim.keyCore kappa pp st omega j =
      Sim.keyCore kappa pp st omega.publicInput (omega.functions j) (omega.values j)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The converted exact setup algorithm is the original semi-adaptive setup.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSim_setup (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) :
    Sim.toSim.setup kappa pp = Sim.setup kappa pp

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Converted exact ciphertext simulation is precisely public-input-only simulation.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSim_enc (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (st : Sim.St kappa pp) (omega : S.Omega kappa pp) :
    Sim.toSim.enc kappa pp st omega = Sim.enc kappa pp st omega.publicInput

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Converted exact key simulation is precisely the indexed function/scalar simulation.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSim_key (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (st : Sim.St kappa pp) (omega : S.Omega kappa pp) (j : Fin omega.count) :
    Sim.toSim.key kappa pp st omega j =
      Sim.key kappa pp st omega.publicInput (omega.functions j) (omega.values j)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The first machine uses the first block of the composed adversary's tape.
This is deterministic coin-layout glue, not a sampler or an assumption reduction.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def firstCoins (A : TwoStage) (kappa : ℕ) (r : List Bool) : A.first.Coins kappa :=
  fun i => r.getD i.val false

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The first coin block is read from the tape's initial coordinates.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem firstCoins_eq (A : TwoStage) (kappa : ℕ) (r : List Bool) :
    A.firstCoins kappa r = fun i => r.getD i.val false

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The second machine uses the disjoint block immediately after the first coins.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def secondCoins (A : TwoStage) (kappa : ℕ) (r : List Bool) : A.second.Coins kappa :=
  fun i => r.getD (A.first.coinLen kappa + i.val) false

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The second coin block starts exactly after the first machine's coin count.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem secondCoins_eq (A : TwoStage) (kappa : ℕ) (r : List Bool) :
    A.secondCoins kappa r = fun i => r.getD (A.first.coinLen kappa + i.val) false

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The first machine's commitment depends only on its coin block, before it can
observe pp or pk. [GJLS21, Definition 4.3].
The commitment is the canonical parser of the first machine's activation.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saCommitment_eq (A : TwoStage) (C : FnClass) (q : PolyExpr) (kappa : ℕ)
    (r : List Bool) : A.saCommitment C q kappa r =
    Commitment.decode C q kappa (A.first.runAt kappa [] (A.firstCoins kappa r))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The next move first asks the committed challenge, then each committed key in
order, and finally runs the second machine on the canonical public view. Failed
challenge answers return false. No ciphertext or key encoding is inverted.
[GJLS21, Definition 4.3; Wee20, §2.2, p.5], exact typed embedding.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def saNext {C : FnClass} {S : FEScheme.Raw C} (A : TwoStage) (q : PolyExpr)
    (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) (pk : S.MPK kappa pp)
    (r : List Bool) (hist : QueryLog (S.saSpec kappa)) : Move (S.saSpec kappa) Bool :=
  let a := A.saCommitment C q kappa r
  match hist with
  | [] => S.saChallengeMove kappa a.publicInput a.privateInput
  | e :: es =>
    match S.saCTPayload kappa e.1 e.2.2 with
    | none => .ret false
    | some ct =>
      if h : es.length < q.eval kappa then
        S.saKeyMove kappa (a.functions ⟨es.length, h⟩)
      else
        let keys := es.filterMap fun entry => S.saSKPayload kappa entry.1 entry.2.2
        .ret (A.second.distinguisherL kappa
          (S.viewWordBits a pp (S.encMPK kappa pp pk) keys ct) (A.secondCoins kappa r))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: On the empty history the embedded adversary asks its committed challenge.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saNext_nil {C : FnClass} {S : FEScheme.Raw C} (A : TwoStage) (q : PolyExpr)
    (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) (pk : S.MPK kappa pp) (r : List Bool) :
    A.saNext (S := S) q kappa pp pk r [] =
      S.saChallengeMove kappa (A.saCommitment C q kappa r).publicInput
        (A.saCommitment C q kappa r).privateInput

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
After the challenge the embedded adversary reads its payload, requests the
next committed key, or supplies the collected wire payloads to the second machine.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saNext_cons {C : FnClass} {S : FEScheme.Raw C} (A : TwoStage) (q : PolyExpr)
    (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) (pk : S.MPK kappa pp) (r : List Bool)
    (e : Sigma fun i => (S.saSpec kappa).dom i × (S.saSpec kappa).rng i)
    (es : QueryLog (S.saSpec kappa)) :
    A.saNext (S := S) q kappa pp pk r (e :: es) =
      let a

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
A committed machine pair becomes a typed semi-adaptive adversary with a total
budget of q+1 calls and concatenated independent coin blocks. The first stage
ignores pp and pk; the second sees exactly the specified public view.
[GJLS21, Definition 4.3; Wee20, §2.2, p.5]. This constructs no oracle NUPPT.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def toSA {C : FnClass} {S : FEScheme.Raw C} (A : TwoStage) (q : PolyExpr) : S.SAAdv where
  coins := .add A.first.coins A.second.coins
  budget := .add q (PolyExpr.const 1)
  next := A.saNext (S := S) q

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The composed tape has the sum of the two original coin polynomials.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSA_coins {C : FnClass} {S : FEScheme.Raw C} (A : TwoStage) (q : PolyExpr) :
    (A.toSA (S := S) q).coins = .add A.first.coins A.second.coins

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The total query budget is exactly one challenge plus q keys.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSA_budget {C : FnClass} {S : FEScheme.Raw C} (A : TwoStage) (q : PolyExpr) :
    (A.toSA (S := S) q).budget = .add q (PolyExpr.const 1)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The embedded next move is the explicit committed protocol above.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSA_next {C : FnClass} {S : FEScheme.Raw C} (A : TwoStage) (q : PolyExpr) :
    (A.toSA (S := S) q).next = A.saNext (S := S) q

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The embedded adversary uses the existing bounded interpreter at q+1 total calls.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem toSA_run {C : FnClass} {S : FEScheme.Raw C} (A : TwoStage) (q : PolyExpr)
    (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) (pk : S.MPK kappa pp) (r : List Bool) :
    (A.toSA (S := S) q).run kappa pp pk r =
      buildComp (A.saNext (S := S) q kappa pp pk r) false (q.eval kappa + 1) []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The committed and derived semi-adaptive games have exactly the same laws.
[GJLS21, Definition 4.3; Wee20, §2.2, p.5]. This is expectation equality, since
independent draws occur in different syntactic orders.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem expect_simGame_eq_saGame (Sim : FEScheme.Raw.SASimulator.Raw S) (A : TwoStage)
    (q : PolyExpr) (real : Bool) (kappa : ℕ) (test : Bool → ℝ) :
    ProbComp.expect (S.simGame Sim.toSim A q real kappa) test =
      ProbComp.expect (S.saGame Sim (A.toSA (S := S) q) real kappa) test

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The committed simulation advantage equals the semi-adaptive advantage of its
explicit typed embedding, with no loss. [GJLS21, Definition 4.3; Wee20, §2.2].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem simAdv_eq_saSimAdv (Sim : FEScheme.Raw.SASimulator.Raw S) (A : TwoStage)
    (q : PolyExpr) (kappa : ℕ) :
    S.simAdv Sim.toSim A q kappa = S.saSimAdv Sim (A.toSA (S := S) q) kappa

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The challenger retains the committed public/private pair to evaluate each
adaptive query's allowed scalar. [Wee20, §2.2, p.5].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
structure SAChallenge (C : FnClass) (kappa : ℕ) where
  /-- The public challenge input. -/
  publicInput : Fin (C.pubLen.eval kappa) → Bool
  /-- The private challenge input, hidden from the simulator. -/
  privateInput : Fin (C.privLen.eval kappa) → Bool

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The real challenger records whether its one challenge has occurred.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: abbrev SAState (S : FEScheme.Raw C) (kappa : ℕ) : Type := Option (SAChallenge C kappa)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Real state is the optional committed challenge.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: theorem saState_eq (kappa : ℕ) : S.SAState kappa = Option (SAChallenge C kappa)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The ideal challenger retains simulator state separately from its hidden input pair.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
abbrev SAIdealState (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) :
    Type := Sim.St kappa pp × S.SAState kappa

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Ideal state is exactly the simulator state paired with the challenger commitment.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saIdealState_eq (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (kappa : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) :
    S.SAIdealState Sim kappa pp = (Sim.St kappa pp × S.SAState kappa)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Adapt typed challenge/key handlers to the library bit specification, using the
shared optional-answer encoding. Technical oracle-interface glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def saImpl {sigma : Type} (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (challenge : (Fin (C.pubLen.eval kappa) → Bool) →
      (Fin (C.privLen.eval kappa) → Bool) → sigma → ProbComp (Option (S.CT kappa pp) × sigma))
    (key : (Fin (C.fnLen.eval kappa) → Bool) → sigma →
      ProbComp (Option (S.SK kappa pp) × sigma)) :
    QueryImpl (S.saSpec kappa) sigma unifSpec
  | 0, xy, st => (challenge (S.saSplitChallenge kappa xy).1
      (S.saSplitChallenge kappa xy).2 st).bind fun o =>
      .pure (S.saCTAnswer kappa pp o.1, o.2)
  | 1, f, st => (key (S.saKeyFunction kappa f) st).bind fun o =>
      .pure (S.saSKAnswer kappa pp o.1, o.2)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Oracle zero calls the typed challenge handler and encodes its optional answer.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saImpl_zero_onSpec {sigma : Type} (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (challenge : (Fin (C.pubLen.eval kappa) → Bool) →
      (Fin (C.privLen.eval kappa) → Bool) → sigma → ProbComp (Option (S.CT kappa pp) × sigma))
    (key : (Fin (C.fnLen.eval kappa) → Bool) → sigma →
      ProbComp (Option (S.SK kappa pp) × sigma))
    (xy : (S.saSpec kappa).dom 0) (st : sigma) :
    S.saImpl kappa pp challenge key 0 xy st =
      (challenge (S.saSplitChallenge kappa xy).1 (S.saSplitChallenge kappa xy).2 st).bind
        fun o => .pure (S.saCTAnswer kappa pp o.1, o.2)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Oracle one calls the typed key handler and encodes its optional answer.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saImpl_one_onSpec {sigma : Type} (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (challenge : (Fin (C.pubLen.eval kappa) → Bool) →
      (Fin (C.privLen.eval kappa) → Bool) → sigma → ProbComp (Option (S.CT kappa pp) × sigma))
    (key : (Fin (C.fnLen.eval kappa) → Bool) → sigma →
      ProbComp (Option (S.SK kappa pp) × sigma))
    (f : (S.saSpec kappa).dom 1) (st : sigma) :
    S.saImpl kappa pp challenge key 1 f st =
      (key (S.saKeyFunction kappa f) st).bind fun o =>
        .pure (S.saSKAnswer kappa pp o.1, o.2)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The real challenge handler accepts the first input pair and rejects repeats.
[Wee20, §2.2, p.5].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def realSAChallenge (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (pk : S.MPK kappa pp) (x : Fin (C.pubLen.eval kappa) → Bool)
    (y : Fin (C.privLen.eval kappa) → Bool) :
    S.SAState kappa → ProbComp (Option (S.CT kappa pp) × S.SAState kappa)
  | none => (S.enc kappa pp pk x y).bind fun ct => .pure (some ct, some ⟨x, y⟩)
  | some a => .pure (none, some a)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The first real challenge produces an honest ciphertext and records its inputs.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem realSAChallenge_none (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (pk : S.MPK kappa pp) (x : Fin (C.pubLen.eval kappa) → Bool)
    (y : Fin (C.privLen.eval kappa) → Bool) :
    S.realSAChallenge kappa pp pk x y none =
      (S.enc kappa pp pk x y).bind fun ct => .pure (some ct, some ⟨x, y⟩)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A repeated real challenge fails and leaves the commitment unchanged.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem realSAChallenge_some (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (pk : S.MPK kappa pp) (x : Fin (C.pubLen.eval kappa) → Bool)
    (y : Fin (C.privLen.eval kappa) → Bool) (a : SAChallenge C kappa) :
    S.realSAChallenge kappa pp pk x y (some a) = .pure (none, some a)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The real key handler rejects calls before the challenge and otherwise samples
an honest key for the adaptive function query. [Wee20, §2.2, p.5].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def realSAKey (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (msk : S.MSK kappa pp) (f : Fin (C.fnLen.eval kappa) → Bool) :
    S.SAState kappa → ProbComp (Option (S.SK kappa pp) × S.SAState kappa)
  | none => .pure (none, none)
  | some a => (S.keyGen kappa pp msk f).bind fun sk => .pure (some sk, some a)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A real key request before the challenge fails.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem realSAKey_none (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (msk : S.MSK kappa pp) (f : Fin (C.fnLen.eval kappa) → Bool) :
    S.realSAKey kappa pp msk f none = .pure (none, none)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A real key request after the challenge samples its honest key.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem realSAKey_some (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (msk : S.MSK kappa pp) (f : Fin (C.fnLen.eval kappa) → Bool)
    (a : SAChallenge C kappa) : S.realSAKey kappa pp msk f (some a) =
    (S.keyGen kappa pp msk f).bind fun sk => .pure (some sk, some a)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The ideal challenge handler sends only x to the simulator and keeps y in
challenger state for future scalar evaluations. [Wee20, §2.2, p.5].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def idealSAChallenge (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (kappa : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) (x : Fin (C.pubLen.eval kappa) → Bool)
    (y : Fin (C.privLen.eval kappa) → Bool) :
    S.SAIdealState Sim kappa pp →
      ProbComp (Option (S.CT kappa pp) × S.SAIdealState Sim kappa pp)
  | (st, none) => (Sim.enc kappa pp st x).bind fun o => .pure (some o.1, o.2, some ⟨x, y⟩)
  | (st, some a) => .pure (none, st, some a)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The first ideal challenge uses public-input-only simulation and records the pair.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem idealSAChallenge_none (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (kappa : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) (x : Fin (C.pubLen.eval kappa) → Bool)
    (y : Fin (C.privLen.eval kappa) → Bool) (st : Sim.St kappa pp) :
    S.idealSAChallenge Sim kappa pp x y (st, none) =
      (Sim.enc kappa pp st x).bind fun o => .pure (some o.1, o.2, some ⟨x, y⟩)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: A repeated ideal challenge fails without changing either state component.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem idealSAChallenge_some (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (kappa : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) (x : Fin (C.pubLen.eval kappa) → Bool)
    (y : Fin (C.privLen.eval kappa) → Bool) (st : Sim.St kappa pp)
    (a : SAChallenge C kappa) :
    S.idealSAChallenge Sim kappa pp x y (st, some a) = .pure (none, st, some a)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The ideal key handler supplies exactly the function's allowed scalar to the
stateful simulator, rejecting queries before the challenge. [Wee20, §2.2, p.5].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def idealSAKey (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (kappa : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) (f : Fin (C.fnLen.eval kappa) → Bool) :
    S.SAIdealState Sim kappa pp →
      ProbComp (Option (S.SK kappa pp) × S.SAIdealState Sim kappa pp)
  | (st, none) => .pure (none, st, none)
  | (st, some a) =>
    (Sim.key kappa pp st a.publicInput f
      (C.eval kappa (S.cprm kappa pp) f a.publicInput a.privateInput)).bind fun o =>
        .pure (some o.1, o.2, some a)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: An ideal key request before the challenge fails.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem idealSAKey_none (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (kappa : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) (f : Fin (C.fnLen.eval kappa) → Bool)
    (st : Sim.St kappa pp) :
    S.idealSAKey Sim kappa pp f (st, none) = .pure (none, st, none)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: An ideal key request after the challenge uses precisely its allowed scalar.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem idealSAKey_some (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (kappa : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) (f : Fin (C.fnLen.eval kappa) → Bool)
    (st : Sim.St kappa pp) (a : SAChallenge C kappa) :
    S.idealSAKey Sim kappa pp f (st, some a) =
      (Sim.key kappa pp st a.publicInput f
        (C.eval kappa (S.cprm kappa pp) f a.publicInput a.privateInput)).bind fun o =>
          .pure (some o.1, o.2, some a)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The real oracle implementation is the wire adapter of the honest typed handlers.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def realSAImpl (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (pk : S.MPK kappa pp) (msk : S.MSK kappa pp) :
    QueryImpl (S.saSpec kappa) (S.SAState kappa) unifSpec :=
  S.saImpl kappa pp (S.realSAChallenge kappa pp pk) (S.realSAKey kappa pp msk)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The real implementation is exactly the displayed adapter.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem realSAImpl_eq (kappa : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa)
    (pk : S.MPK kappa pp) (msk : S.MSK kappa pp) : S.realSAImpl kappa pp pk msk =
    S.saImpl kappa pp (S.realSAChallenge kappa pp pk) (S.realSAKey kappa pp msk)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The ideal oracle implementation adapts its stateful typed simulation handlers.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def idealSAImpl (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (kappa : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) :
    QueryImpl (S.saSpec kappa) (S.SAIdealState Sim kappa pp) unifSpec :=
  S.saImpl kappa pp (S.idealSAChallenge Sim kappa pp) (S.idealSAKey Sim kappa pp)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The ideal implementation is exactly the displayed adapter.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem idealSAImpl_eq (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (kappa : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams S.G kappa) : S.idealSAImpl Sim kappa pp =
    S.saImpl kappa pp (S.idealSAChallenge Sim kappa pp) (S.idealSAKey Sim kappa pp)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The semi-adaptive game first generates pp and the public key, then runs the
bounded adversary with one independent coin tape. True selects the real experiment.
[Wee20, §2.2, p.5].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def saGame (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (A : S.SAAdv) (real : Bool)
    (kappa : ℕ) : ProbComp Bool :=
  (S.pubGen kappa).bind fun pp =>
    if real then
      (S.setup kappa pp).bind fun k =>
      (ProbComp.sample (Fin (A.coins.eval kappa) → Bool)).bind fun r =>
        Prod.fst <$> simulate (S.realSAImpl kappa pp k.1 k.2)
          (A.run kappa pp k.1 (List.ofFn r)) none
    else
      (Sim.setup kappa pp).bind fun k =>
      (ProbComp.sample (Fin (A.coins.eval kappa) → Bool)).bind fun r =>
        Prod.fst <$> simulate (S.idealSAImpl Sim kappa pp)
          (A.run kappa pp k.1 (List.ofFn r)) (k.2, none)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The complete game is the displayed exact stateful experiment.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saGame_eq (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (A : S.SAAdv) (real : Bool) (kappa : ℕ) :
    S.saGame Sim A real kappa = (S.pubGen kappa).bind fun pp =>
      if real then
        (S.setup kappa pp).bind fun k =>
        (ProbComp.sample (Fin (A.coins.eval kappa) → Bool)).bind fun r =>
          Prod.fst <$> simulate (S.realSAImpl kappa pp k.1 k.2)
            (A.run kappa pp k.1 (List.ofFn r)) none
      else
        (Sim.setup kappa pp).bind fun k =>
        (ProbComp.sample (Fin (A.coins.eval kappa) → Bool)).bind fun r =>
          Prod.fst <$> simulate (S.idealSAImpl Sim kappa pp)
            (A.run kappa pp k.1 (List.ofFn r)) (k.2, none)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Semi-adaptive simulation advantage is the common two-experiment advantage.
[Wee20, §2.2, p.5].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def saSimAdv (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (A : S.SAAdv) (kappa : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  advantage (S.saGame Sim A true kappa) (S.saGame Sim A false kappa)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Semi-adaptive advantage is the displayed real/ideal difference.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saSimAdv_eq (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) (A : S.SAAdv) (kappa : ℕ) :
    S.saSimAdv Sim A kappa =
      advantage (S.saGame Sim A true kappa) (S.saGame Sim A false kappa)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
A specified raw simulator gives negligible advantage against every oracle
NUPPT and polynomial total-call budget. [Wee20, §2.2, p.5].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def SASimSecureWith (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) : Prop :=
  ∀ A : NUPPT, ∀ q : PolyExpr, Negligible (S.saSimAdv Sim (toSAAdv (S := S) A q))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Raw semi-adaptive security is the displayed negligible-advantage condition.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saSimSecureWith_iff (Sim : SASimulator.Raw S) :
    S.SASimSecureWith Sim ↔
      ∀ A : NUPPT, ∀ q : PolyExpr, Negligible (S.saSimAdv Sim (toSAAdv (S := S) A q))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Semi-adaptive simulation security names one efficient simulator before all
oracle machines and budgets. [Wee20, §2.2, p.5].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header: def SASimSecure : Prop := ∃ Sim : SASimulator S, S.SASimSecureWith Sim.toRaw

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Semi-adaptive security quantifies over the efficient simulator interface.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saSimSecure_iff :
