def crossLeakRight (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn)
    (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) (f : Fn κ pp.orderParam)
    (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order)
    (y1 : Fin (n1.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) (y2 : Fin (n2.eval κ) → pp.group.G)
    (mu : pp.group.G) : pp.group.G :=
  groupDot (fun i => let j := finProdFinEquiv.symm i; y2 j.2 ^ (y1 j.1).val)
    (PG.eval κ pp.orderParam f x) * mu⁻¹

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Right tensor leakage uses only known scalar powers of the supplied group vector.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem crossLeakRight_eq (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn)
    (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) (f : Fn κ pp.orderParam)
    (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order)
    (y1 : Fin (n1.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) (y2 : Fin (n2.eval κ) → pp.group.G)
    (mu : pp.group.G) : crossLeakRight G n1 n2 PG κ pp f x y1 y2 mu =
      groupDot (fun i => let j := finProdFinEquiv.symm i; y2 j.2 ^ (y1 j.1).val)
        (PG.eval κ pp.orderParam f x) * mu⁻¹

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Replace the first vector using MDDH¹_{2,n1}. The public first matrix and ciphertext
first vector remain GROUP data; all key leakage uses known scalar y2
[Wee20, §3.3, pp. 7–8, Game 2 to Game 3].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def red2Handler (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 q : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (κ : ℕ)
    (c : G.MDDHChallenge (PolyExpr.const 1) n1 κ) (m : Masks G n1 n2 κ c.pp)
    (st : Linear.SimState G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ c.pp)
    (ω : Linear.SecurityDraw G PG (piDim n1 n2) q κ c.pp) :
    ∀ i, (saSpec G n1 n2 PG κ c.pp).dom i → SAState G ℓ n1 n2 κ c.pp →
      (saSpec G n1 n2 PG κ c.pp).rng i × SAState G ℓ n1 n2 κ c.pp :=
  let A2 := c.pp.group.expMat c.pp.generator m.A2
  let M := mixGroup G n1 n2 κ c.pp c.matrixᵀ A2
  let first := fun (msg : Challenge G ℓ n1 n2 κ c.pp) => (fun i => c.response i (0 : Fin 1)) *
    c.pp.group.expVec c.pp.generator msg.2.1
  let second := fun (msg : Challenge G ℓ n1 n2 κ c.pp) => Matrix.vecMul m.s2 m.A2 + msg.2.2
  protocolHandler G n1 n2 PG (q.eval κ) κ c.pp
    (fun msg => ⟨first msg, c.pp.group.expVec c.pp.generator (second msg),
      Linear.simEncCore G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ c.pp st msg.1⟩)
    (fun j msg f => ⟨f, ⟨M, Linear.simKeyCore G PG (piDim n1 n2) κ c.pp st f M msg.1
      (crossLeakLeft G n1 n2 PG κ c.pp f msg.1 (first msg) (second msg)
        (c.pp.generator ^ (value G n1 n2 PG κ c.pp f msg.1 msg.2.1 msg.2.2).val))
      (Linear.simKeyAt G PG (piDim n1 n2) q κ c.pp ω j f)⟩⟩)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The first replacement handler is the displayed pure protocol.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem red2Handler_eq (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 q : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (κ : ℕ)
    (c : G.MDDHChallenge (PolyExpr.const 1) n1 κ) (m : Masks G n1 n2 κ c.pp)
    (st : Linear.SimState G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ c.pp)
    (ω : Linear.SecurityDraw G PG (piDim n1 n2) q κ c.pp) :
    red2Handler G n1 n2 q PG κ c m st ω =
      let A2

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Replace the second vector using MDDH¹_{2,n2}; y1 is already a known uniform scalar
advice vector [Wee20, §3.3, pp. 7–8, Game 3 to Game 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def red3Handler (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 q : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (κ : ℕ)
    (c : G.MDDHChallenge (PolyExpr.const 1) n2 κ) (m : Masks G n1 n2 κ c.pp)
    (st : Linear.SimState G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ c.pp)
    (ω : Linear.SecurityDraw G PG (piDim n1 n2) q κ c.pp) :
    ∀ i, (saSpec G n1 n2 PG κ c.pp).dom i → SAState G ℓ n1 n2 κ c.pp →
      (saSpec G n1 n2 PG κ c.pp).rng i × SAState G ℓ n1 n2 κ c.pp :=
  let A1 := c.pp.group.expMat c.pp.generator m.A1
  let M := mixGroup G n1 n2 κ c.pp A1 c.matrixᵀ
  let second := fun (msg : Challenge G ℓ n1 n2 κ c.pp) => (fun i => c.response i (0 : Fin 1)) *
    c.pp.group.expVec c.pp.generator msg.2.2
  protocolHandler G n1 n2 PG (q.eval κ) κ c.pp
    (fun msg => ⟨c.pp.group.expVec c.pp.generator m.y1, second msg,
      Linear.simEncCore G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ c.pp st msg.1⟩)
    (fun j msg f => ⟨f, ⟨M, Linear.simKeyCore G PG (piDim n1 n2) κ c.pp st f M msg.1
      (crossLeakRight G n1 n2 PG κ c.pp f msg.1 m.y1 (second msg)
        (c.pp.generator ^ (value G n1 n2 PG κ c.pp f msg.1 msg.2.1 msg.2.2).val))
      (Linear.simKeyAt G PG (piDim n1 n2) q κ c.pp ω j f)⟩⟩)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The second replacement handler is the displayed pure protocol.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem red3Handler_eq (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 q : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (κ : ℕ)
    (c : G.MDDHChallenge (PolyExpr.const 1) n2 κ) (m : Masks G n1 n2 κ c.pp)
    (st : Linear.SimState G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ c.pp)
    (ω : Linear.SecurityDraw G PG (piDim n1 n2) q κ c.pp) :
    red3Handler G n1 n2 q PG κ c m st ω =
      let A1

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The first outer L2 reduction fixes the finite advice and runs the original typed
adversary without sampling [Wee20, §3.3, pp. 7–8, Game 2 to Game 3].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def red2 (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (A : SAAdv G n1 n2 PG)
    (ω : ∀ κ, Advice n1 n2 A.budget PG p κ) (κ : ℕ)
    (c : G.MDDHChallenge (PolyExpr.const 1) n1 κ) (r : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  let tape := adviceDraw G n1 n2 A.budget PG p hp κ c.pp (ω κ)
  let m := masksAt G n1 n2 κ c.pp tape.1
  let ctx := Linear.simSetupCore G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ c.pp
    (Linear.setupAt G PG (piDim n1 n2) A.budget κ c.pp tape.2)
  let pk : MPK G ℓ n1 n2 κ c.pp :=
    ⟨c.matrixᵀ, c.pp.group.expMat c.pp.generator m.A2, ctx.1⟩
  [(runDet (A.next κ c.pp pk r) false
    (red2Handler G n1 n2 A.budget PG κ c m ctx.2 tape.2)
    (A.budget.eval κ) [] ⟨none, 0⟩).1]

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The first L2 reduction exposes its exact advice, public key and runDet result.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem red2_eq (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (A : SAAdv G n1 n2 PG)
    (ω : ∀ κ, Advice n1 n2 A.budget PG p κ) (κ : ℕ)
    (c : G.MDDHChallenge (PolyExpr.const 1) n1 κ) (r : List Bool) :
    red2 G n1 n2 PG p hp A ω κ c r =
      let tape

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The second outer L2 reduction fixes its independent finite advice and never samples
[Wee20, §3.3, pp. 7–8, Game 3 to Game 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def red3 (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (A : SAAdv G n1 n2 PG)
    (ω : ∀ κ, Advice n1 n2 A.budget PG p κ) (κ : ℕ)
    (c : G.MDDHChallenge (PolyExpr.const 1) n2 κ) (r : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  let tape := adviceDraw G n1 n2 A.budget PG p hp κ c.pp (ω κ)
  let m := masksAt G n1 n2 κ c.pp tape.1
  let ctx := Linear.simSetupCore G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ c.pp
    (Linear.setupAt G PG (piDim n1 n2) A.budget κ c.pp tape.2)
  let pk : MPK G ℓ n1 n2 κ c.pp :=
    ⟨c.pp.group.expMat c.pp.generator m.A1, c.matrixᵀ, ctx.1⟩
  [(runDet (A.next κ c.pp pk r) false
    (red3Handler G n1 n2 A.budget PG κ c m ctx.2 tape.2)
    (A.budget.eval κ) [] ⟨none, 0⟩).1]

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The second L2 reduction exposes its exact advice, public key and runDet result.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem red3_eq (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (A : SAAdv G n1 n2 PG)
    (ω : ∀ κ, Advice n1 n2 A.budget PG p κ) (κ : ℕ)
    (c : G.MDDHChallenge (PolyExpr.const 1) n2 κ) (r : List Bool) :
    red3 G n1 n2 PG p hp A ω κ c r =
      let tape

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The mask advice used by the derived Π adversary has its explicit polynomial word
bound. Fixed-advice bookkeeping.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem length_maskAdviceEnc_le (G : BilinearGen) (n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (κ : ℕ) (ω : MaskAdvice n1 n2 p κ) :
    (maskAdviceEnc G n1 n2 p hp κ ω).length ≤ (maskAdviceLen G n1 n2).eval κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The derived adversary's mask advice word is injective. Fixed-advice bookkeeping.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem maskAdviceEnc_injective (G : BilinearGen) (n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (κ : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (maskAdviceEnc G n1 n2 p hp κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Outer advice encoding is polynomially bounded. Fixed-advice bookkeeping.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem length_adviceEnc_le (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 q : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (κ : ℕ) (ω : Advice n1 n2 q PG p κ) :
    (adviceEnc G n1 n2 q PG p hp κ ω).length ≤ (adviceLen G n1 n2 q PG).eval κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Full advice encoding is injective. Fixed-advice bookkeeping.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem adviceEnc_injective (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 q : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (κ : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (adviceEnc G n1 n2 q PG p hp κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Left mixed leakage equals the scalar tensor leakage whenever the supplied group
vector is the encoding of a KNOWN scalar vector [Wee20, §3.3, pp. 7–8].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem crossLeakLeft_known (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn)
    (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) (f : Fn κ pp.orderParam)
    (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order)
    (y1 : Fin (n1.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order)
    (y2 : Fin (n2.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) (mu : pp.group.G) :
    crossLeakLeft G n1 n2 PG κ pp f x (pp.group.expVec pp.generator y1) y2 mu =
      pp.generator ^ (value G n1 n2 PG κ pp f x y1 y2).val * mu⁻¹

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Right mixed leakage equals the scalar tensor leakage for a KNOWN scalar y2
[Wee20, §3.3, pp. 7–8].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem crossLeakRight_known (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn)
    (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) (f : Fn κ pp.orderParam)
    (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order)
    (y1 : Fin (n1.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order)
    (y2 : Fin (n2.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) (mu : pp.group.G) :
    crossLeakRight G n1 n2 PG κ pp f x y1 (pp.group.expVec pp.generator y2) mu =
      pp.generator ^ (value G n1 n2 PG κ pp f x y1 y2).val * mu⁻¹

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The pure derived adversary exactly reproduces the honest or Π-simulated outer
endpoint for every fixed tape and coin string [Wee20, §3.3, Game 0 to Game 1, p. 7].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem derived_run_endpoint (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (A : SAAdv G n1 n2 PG)
    (φ : ∀ κ, MaskAdvice n1 n2 p κ) (ideal : Bool) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ)
    (ω : Linear.SecurityDraw G PG (piDim n1 n2) A.budget κ pp) (r : List Bool) :
    runGameDet G n1 n2 PG A (if ideal then 1 else 0) κ pp
      (maskAdviceDraw G n1 n2 p hp κ pp (φ κ), ω) r =
    Linear.runGameDet G PG (piDim n1 n2) (toLinear G n1 n2 PG p hp A φ)
      (if ideal then 5 else 0) false κ pp ω r

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Fixing only outer scalar masks gives an explicit derived Π adversary whose ACTUAL
fresh-law simulation advantage bounds the first outer hop [Wee20, §3.3, pp. 7–8].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem game0_game1_le (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (A : SAAdv G n1 n2 PG) :
    ∃ φ : ∀ κ, MaskAdvice n1 n2 p κ, ∀ κ,
      advantage (game G n1 n2 PG A 0 κ) (game G n1 n2 PG A 1 κ) ≤
        Linear.freshSaSimAdv G PG (piDim n1 n2) (toLinear G n1 n2 PG p hp A φ) κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Equation (5) rewrites the actual source-group signal leakage without changing any
transcript [Wee20, §3.1, (5), p. 6; §3.3, Game 1 to Game 2, p. 7].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem game1_game2_accept (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn)
    (A : SAAdv G n1 n2 PG) (κ : ℕ) :
    accept (game G n1 n2 PG A 1 κ) = accept (game G n1 n2 PG A 2 κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
One MDDH¹_{2,n1} realiser bounds the first outer mask replacement
[Wee20, §3.3, Game 2 to Game 3, p. 8].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem game2_game3_le (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (A : SAAdv G n1 n2 PG) :
    ∃ ω : ∀ κ, Advice n1 n2 A.budget PG p κ, ∀ D : NUPPT,
      D.RealizesOn (G.mddhEnc (PolyExpr.const 1) n1) A.coins (red2 G n1 n2 PG p hp A ω) →
      ∀ κ, advantage (game G n1 n2 PG A 2 κ) (game G n1 n2 PG A 3 κ) ≤
        G.mddhAdv (PolyExpr.const 1) n1 D κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
One MDDH¹_{2,n2} realiser bounds the second outer mask replacement
[Wee20, §3.3, Game 3 to Game 4, p. 8].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem game3_game4_le (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (A : SAAdv G n1 n2 PG) :
    ∃ ω : ∀ κ, Advice n1 n2 A.budget PG p κ, ∀ D : NUPPT,
      D.RealizesOn (G.mddhEnc (PolyExpr.const 1) n2) A.coins (red3 G n1 n2 PG p hp A ω) →
      ∀ κ, advantage (game G n1 n2 PG A 3 κ) (game G n1 n2 PG A 4 κ) ≤
        G.mddhAdv (PolyExpr.const 1) n2 D κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The two padded outer endpoints have the acceptance laws of the ACTUAL fresh raw
setup/encryption/key generation and stateful simulator [Wee20, §3.1–§3.2, pp. 6–7].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saGame_eq_freshSaGame (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn)
    (A : SAAdv G n1 n2 PG) (ideal : Bool) (κ : ℕ) :
    accept (saGame G n1 n2 PG A ideal κ) =
      accept (freshSaGame G n1 n2 PG A ideal κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The actual fresh and padded outer advantages coincide [Wee20, §3.3, pp. 7–8].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem saSimAdv_eq_freshSaSimAdv (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn)
    (A : SAAdv G n1 n2 PG) (κ : ℕ) :
    saSimAdv G n1 n2 PG A κ = freshSaSimAdv G n1 n2 PG A κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
For every typed outer adversary, fixed scalar advice makes EVERY four realising
machines satisfy the explicit ACTUAL raw semi-adaptive simulation bound
[Wee20, §3, p. 6, main security claim with §3.3, pp. 7–8 and Appendix B, Theorem 1].
The single statistical term is Π's exact unconditioned-basis failure probability.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem quadratic_saSimAdv_le (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (A : SAAdv G n1 n2 PG) :
    ∃ φ : ∀ κ, MaskAdvice n1 n2 p κ,
    ∃ ωPi : Fin 2 → ∀ κ, Linear.Advice PG (piDim n1 n2) A.budget p κ,
    ∃ ωOuter : Fin 2 → ∀ κ, Advice n1 n2 A.budget PG p κ,
    ∀ D : Fin 4 → NUPPT,
      (D 0).RealizesOn (G.mddhEnc (PolyExpr.const 1) (PolyExpr.const 3)) A.coins
        (Linear.red0 G PG (piDim n1 n2) p hp (toLinear G n1 n2 PG p hp A φ) (ωPi 0)) →
      (D 1).RealizesOn (G.mddhEnc ℓ (PG.mBound.mul A.budget)) A.coins
        (Linear.red1 G PG (piDim n1 n2) p hp (toLinear G n1 n2 PG p hp A φ) (ωPi 1)) →
      (D 2).RealizesOn (G.mddhEnc (PolyExpr.const 1) n1) A.coins
        (red2 G n1 n2 PG p hp A (ωOuter 0)) →
      (D 3).RealizesOn (G.mddhEnc (PolyExpr.const 1) n2) A.coins
        (red3 G n1 n2 PG p hp A (ωOuter 1)) →
      ∀ κ, freshSaSimAdv G n1 n2 PG A κ ≤
        G.mddhAdv (PolyExpr.const 1) (PolyExpr.const 3) (D 0) κ +
        G.mddhAdv ℓ (PG.mBound.mul A.budget) (D 1) κ +
        G.mddhAdv (PolyExpr.const 1) n1 (D 2) κ + G.mddhAdv (PolyExpr.const 1) n2 (D 3) κ +
        Linear.linearSlack G κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The simulator stores its fixed public group matrix, Π's state and its scalar ciphertext
masks [Wee20, §3.2, p. 7]. Zero masks specify the state before the single challenge.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
structure SimState (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) where
  /-- The fixed public group matrix used in every function key. -/
  matrix : Matrix (Fin ((piDim n1 n2).eval κ)) (Fin ((n1.mul n2).eval κ)) pp.group.G
  /-- The linear simulator's state. -/
  linear : Linear.SimState G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ pp
  /-- The retained first scalar ciphertext mask. -/
  y1 : Fin (n1.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order
  /-- The retained second scalar ciphertext mask. -/
  y2 : Fin (n2.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Simulated setup draws its two scalar public masks and Π's simulator setup draw
[Wee20, §3.2, p. 7, Setup*].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
abbrev SimSetupDraw (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) :=
  Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin (n1.eval κ)) (ZMod pp.group.order) ×
    Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin (n2.eval κ)) (ZMod pp.group.order) ×
    Linear.SimSetupDraw G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ pp

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The setup draw consists of its two outer masks and the linear simulator's draw.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem simSetupDraw_eq (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams G κ) :
    SimSetupDraw G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp =
      (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin (n1.eval κ)) (ZMod pp.group.order) ×
        Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin (n2.eval κ)) (ZMod pp.group.order) ×
        Linear.SimSetupDraw G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ pp)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Simulated encryption draws two independent scalar masks
[Wee20, §3.2, p. 7, Enc*]. The scalar field is the order of the public group.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
abbrev SimEncDraw (G : BilinearGen) (n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) :=
  (Fin (n1.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) × (Fin (n2.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The encryption draw is exactly the pair of scalar vector masks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem simEncDraw_eq (G : BilinearGen) (n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) :
    SimEncDraw G n1 n2 κ pp =
      ((Fin (n1.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) ×
        (Fin (n2.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order))

instance instSimSetupDrawFinite (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G
  κ) :
    Fintype (SimSetupDraw G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) := inferInstance

instance instSimSetupDrawNonempty (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams
  G κ) :
    Nonempty (SimSetupDraw G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) := inferInstance

instance instSimEncDrawFinite (G : BilinearGen) (n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) :
    Fintype (SimEncDraw G n1 n2 κ pp) := inferInstance

instance instSimEncDrawNonempty (G : BilinearGen) (n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ)
  :
    Nonempty (SimEncDraw G n1 n2 κ pp) := inferInstance

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Simulator setup computes its public group matrices and retains the fixed group matrix
with Π's simulator state [Wee20, §3.2, p. 7, Setup*]. The two retained ciphertext masks are
initialized to zero. Π's total scalar inverse also specifies singular setups.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def simSetupCore (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams G κ) (ω : SimSetupDraw G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) :
    MPK G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp × SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp :=
  let A1 := pp.group.expMat pp.generator ω.1
  let A2 := pp.group.expMat pp.generator ω.2.1
  let linear := Linear.simSetupCore G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ pp ω.2.2
  (⟨A1, A2, linear.1⟩, ⟨mixGroup G n1 n2 κ pp A1 A2, linear.2, 0, 0⟩)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Simulated setup exposes its public matrices, linear state and zero initial masks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem simSetupCore_eq (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams G κ) (ω : SimSetupDraw G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) :
    simSetupCore G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp ω =
      let A1

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Simulated encryption publishes its freshly drawn masks and retains their scalars for
later keys [Wee20, §3.2, p. 7, Enc*]. Both group components use the source group, reading
the second component's printed subscript with §3.1.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def simEncCore (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ)
    (st : SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order)
    (ω : SimEncDraw G n1 n2 κ pp) : CT G n1 n2 κ pp × SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp :=
  (⟨pp.group.expVec pp.generator ω.1, pp.group.expVec pp.generator ω.2,
    Linear.simEncCore G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ pp st.linear x⟩,
    ⟨st.matrix, st.linear, ω.1, ω.2⟩)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The ideal ciphertext masks and next state's retained masks are the same draw.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem simEncCore_eq (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams G κ) (st : SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp)
    (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) (ω : SimEncDraw G n1 n2 κ pp) :
    simEncCore G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp st x ω =
      (⟨pp.group.expVec pp.generator ω.1, pp.group.expVec pp.generator ω.2,
        Linear.simEncCore G ℓ (piDim n1 n2) κ pp st.linear x⟩,
        ⟨st.matrix, st.linear, ω.1, ω.2⟩)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The cross-term leakage is `g^((y1⊗y2)f(x)^T) / [mu]` in the SOURCE group
[Wee20, §3.2, p. 7, KeyGen*, read with §3.3, Game 2]. Only the retained scalar masks are
used to form the first factor; the allowed source-group value is inverted as a group element.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def crossLeak (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr) {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type}
    (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ)
    (st : SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) (f : Fn κ pp.orderParam)
    (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) (mu : pp.group.G) : pp.group.G :=
  pp.generator ^ (value G n1 n2 PG κ pp f x st.y1 st.y2).val * mu⁻¹

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The allowed cross term is the displayed quotient in the source group.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem crossLeak_eq (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn)
    (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) (st : SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp)
    (f : Fn κ pp.orderParam) (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) (mu : pp.group.G) :
    crossLeak G n1 n2 PG κ pp st f x mu =
      pp.generator ^ (value G n1 n2 PG κ pp f x st.y1 st.y2).val * mu⁻¹

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
With known scalar allowed value, the simulated cross term represents the corresponding
scalar difference [Wee20, §3.3, p. 7, Game 2 and (5)].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem crossLeak_known_value (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn)
    (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) (st : SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp)
    (f : Fn κ pp.orderParam) (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order)
    (mu : ZMod pp.group.order) :
    crossLeak G n1 n2 PG κ pp st f x (pp.generator ^ mu.val) =
      pp.generator ^ (value G n1 n2 PG κ pp f x st.y1 st.y2 - mu).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Simulator key generation computes the cross-term group value and forwards it to Π's
simulator [Wee20, §3.2, p. 7, KeyGen*]. The fixed public matrix is retained as key metadata.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def simKeyCore (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr) {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type}
    (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ)
    (st : SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) (f : Fn κ pp.orderParam)
    (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) (mu : pp.group.G)
    (ω : Linear.SimKeyDraw G PG κ pp f) : Key G n1 n2 PG κ pp f :=
  ⟨st.matrix, Linear.simKeyCore G PG (piDim n1 n2) κ pp st.linear f st.matrix x
    (crossLeak G n1 n2 PG κ pp st f x mu) ω⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The simulated key forwards precisely the group cross-term value to Π.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem simKeyCore_eq (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn)
    (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) (st : SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp)
    (f : Fn κ pp.orderParam) (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) (mu : pp.group.G)
    (ω : Linear.SimKeyDraw G PG κ pp f) :
    simKeyCore G n1 n2 PG κ pp st f x mu ω =
      ⟨st.matrix, Linear.simKeyCore G PG (piDim n1 n2) κ pp st.linear f st.matrix x
        (crossLeak G n1 n2 PG κ pp st f x mu) ω⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Simulated setup has its exact core-plus-draw law [Wee20, §3.2, p. 7].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def simSetup (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams G κ) : ProbComp (MPK G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp × SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) :=
  (simSetupCore G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp <$> (ProbComp.sample (SimSetupDraw G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Simulated setup is one uniform draw followed by its total core.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem simSetup_eq (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) :
    simSetup G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp =
      (simSetupCore G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp <$> (ProbComp.sample (SimSetupDraw G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Simulated encryption draws the masks once and returns the ciphertext and updated state
[Wee20, §3.2, p. 7].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def simEnc (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ)
    (pp : PublicParams G κ) (st : SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp)
    (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) :
    ProbComp (CT G n1 n2 κ pp × SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) :=
  (simEncCore G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp st x <$> (ProbComp.sample (SimEncDraw G n1 n2 κ pp)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Simulated encryption has the displayed stateful core-plus-draw law.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem simEnc_eq (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ)
    (st : SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) :
    simEnc G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp st x =
      (simEncCore G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp st x <$> (ProbComp.sample (SimEncDraw G n1 n2 κ pp)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Simulated function keys use Π's single function-dependent draw
[Wee20, §3.2, p. 7].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def simKey (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn)
    (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) (st : SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp)
    (f : Fn κ pp.orderParam) (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) (mu : pp.group.G) :
    ProbComp (Key G n1 n2 PG κ pp f) :=
  (simKeyCore G n1 n2 PG κ pp st f x mu <$> (ProbComp.sample (Linear.SimKeyDraw G PG κ pp f)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Simulated keys have the displayed core-plus-draw law.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem simKey_eq (G : BilinearGen) {ℓ : PolyExpr} (n1 n2 : PolyExpr)
    {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type} (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ (n1.mul n2) Fn)
    (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) (st : SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp)
    (f : Fn κ pp.orderParam) (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod pp.group.order) (mu : pp.group.G) :
    simKey G n1 n2 PG κ pp st f x mu =
      (simKeyCore G n1 n2 PG κ pp st f x mu <$> (ProbComp.sample (Linear.SimKeyDraw G PG κ pp f)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The concrete construction's named uniform-efficiency targets are supplied together.
[GJLS21, Definitions 4.1, 4.3 and 4.6; Wee20, Sections 2.2 and 3].
Phase B obligation; not proved in this development.

No field is a hypothesis of raw correctness or a raw security inequality. The L1 target
supplies realisers via the shared theorem; L2 interactive-realiser hypotheses remain
separate statements of the raw security theorems.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
structure Targets (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n : PolyExpr) (d : ℕ) : Prop where
  /-- The five honest-algorithm targets. -/
  scheme : SchemeTargets G ℓ n d
  /-- Both concrete simulators' targets. -/
  simulators : SimTargets G ℓ n d
  /-- Deterministic layered matrix generation and reconstruction targets. -/
  garbling : PGTargets ℓ (n.mul n) d
  /-- The one uniform linear-time encryption target. -/
  linear : LinearEfficient G
  /-- Uniform L1 matrix-DH preprocessing. -/
  mddh : MddhPreTargets G

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: All targets are exactly their displayed conjunction.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem targets_iff (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n : PolyExpr) (d : ℕ) : Targets G ℓ n d ↔
    SchemeTargets G ℓ n d ∧ SimTargets G ℓ n d ∧ PGTargets ℓ (n.mul n) d ∧
      LinearEfficient G ∧ MddhPreTargets G

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The efficient layered primitive is pure assembly of its raw family and two targets
[AGW20, Lemma 2, p.12; IW14, Definition 1 continuation, p.7]. No algorithm is selected or
changed by this assembly.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def layeredPG (ℓ n : PolyExpr) (d : ℕ) (hT : PGTargets ℓ n d) :
    PartialGarbling ℓ n (fun κ p => PolyTensor p (ℓ.eval κ) (n.eval κ) d) where
  toRaw := layeredPG_raw ℓ n d
  lgen_eff := hT.lgen_eff
  rec_eff := hT.rec_eff

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Efficient garbling retains precisely the raw layered algorithms and laws.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem layeredPG_toRaw (ℓ n : PolyExpr) (d : ℕ) (hT : PGTargets ℓ n d) :
    (layeredPG ℓ n d hT).toRaw = layeredPG_raw ℓ n d

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The efficient PHFE primitive is pure assembly of the layered raw scheme and the five
honest-algorithm targets [GJLS21, Definition 4.1; Wee20, Section 3.1].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def wee20PHFE (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n : PolyExpr) (d : ℕ) (hT : SchemeTargets G ℓ n d) :
    FEScheme (phfeClass ℓ n G.wG d) where
  toRaw := wee20PHFE_raw G ℓ n d (layeredPG_raw ℓ (n.mul n) d)
  pubGen_eff := hT.pubGen_eff
  setup_eff := hT.setup_eff
  enc_eff := hT.enc_eff
  keyGen_eff := hT.keyGen_eff
  dec_eff := hT.dec_eff

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Efficient PHFE retains precisely the raw layered construction.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem wee20PHFE_toRaw (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n : PolyExpr) (d : ℕ)
    (hT : SchemeTargets G ℓ n d) :
    (wee20PHFE G ℓ n d hT).toRaw =
      wee20PHFE_raw G ℓ n d (layeredPG_raw ℓ (n.mul n) d)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The efficient committed simulator is pure assembly from its own three concrete
targets [GJLS21, Definition 4.3]. No generic sampler-preprocessing closure is assumed.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def wee20Sim (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n : PolyExpr) (d : ℕ)
    (hT : SimTargets G ℓ n d) :
    FEScheme.Raw.Simulator (wee20PHFE_raw G ℓ n d (layeredPG_raw ℓ (n.mul n) d)) where
  toRaw := wee20Sim_raw G ℓ n d (layeredPG_raw ℓ (n.mul n) d)
  setup_eff := hT.sim_setup_eff
  enc_eff := hT.sim_enc_eff
  key_eff := hT.sim_key_eff

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Efficient committed simulation retains the exact raw simulator.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem wee20Sim_toRaw (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n : PolyExpr) (d : ℕ)
    (hT : SimTargets G ℓ n d) :
    (wee20Sim G ℓ n d hT).toRaw =
      wee20Sim_raw G ℓ n d (layeredPG_raw ℓ (n.mul n) d)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The efficient semi-adaptive simulator is pure assembly from its three concrete
targets [Wee20, Section 2.2]. Its encryption input excludes the private message.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
noncomputable def wee20SASim (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n : PolyExpr) (d : ℕ)
    (hT : SimTargets G ℓ n d) :
    FEScheme.Raw.SASimulator (wee20PHFE_raw G ℓ n d (layeredPG_raw ℓ (n.mul n) d)) where
  toRaw := wee20SASim_raw G ℓ n d (layeredPG_raw ℓ (n.mul n) d)
  setup_eff := hT.sa_setup_eff
  enc_eff := hT.sa_enc_eff
  key_eff := hT.sa_key_eff

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Efficient semi-adaptive simulation retains the exact raw simulator.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem wee20SASim_toRaw (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n : PolyExpr) (d : ℕ)
    (hT : SimTargets G ℓ n d) :
    (wee20SASim G ℓ n d hT).toRaw =
      wee20SASim_raw G ℓ n d (layeredPG_raw ℓ (n.mul n) d)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The assembled public-key width is the exact linear dimension accounting
[Wee20, Section 3.1; GJLS21, Definition 4.6, printed p.22].
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem wee20PHFE_mpkLen_eval (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n : PolyExpr) (d κ : ℕ)
    (hT : SchemeTargets G ℓ n d) :
    (wee20PHFE G ℓ n d hT).mpkLen.eval κ =
      (16 + 24 * n.eval κ + 8 * ℓ.eval κ) * G.wG.eval κ + 10

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The assembled ciphertext has exactly `(6n+5)wG` bits, independently of the
function degree and public-vector length [Wee20, Section 3.1]. The public input is
passed separately and is not counted as part of the ciphertext.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem wee20PHFE_ctLen_eval (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n : PolyExpr) (d κ : ℕ)
    (hT : SchemeTargets G ℓ n d) :
    (wee20PHFE G ℓ n d hT).ctLen.eval κ = (6 * n.eval κ + 5) * G.wG.eval κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Layered matrix generation and reconstruction satisfy the deterministic efficiency
clauses [AGW20, Lemma 2, p.12; IW14, Definition 1 continuation, p.7].
Phase B obligation; not proved in this development.

Each witness precedes κ and the arbitrary positive modulus, which is part of the input.
The definition imposes no sampling contract and no per-parameter modulus computation.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
structure PGTargets : Prop where
  /-- One uniform map computes both matrices from the supplied modulus and tensor. -/
  lgen_eff : ∃ a : List Bool → List Bool, PolyTimeComputable a ∧
    ∀ κ (p : ℕ+) (f : PolyTensor p (ℓ.eval κ) (n.eval κ) d),
      a ((PG).lgenInput κ p f) = (PG).encLgen κ p f
  /-- One uniform map computes reconstruction from the supplied modulus and public input. -/
  rec_eff : ∃ a : List Bool → List Bool, PolyTimeComputable a ∧
    ∀ κ (p : ℕ+) (f : PolyTensor p (ℓ.eval κ) (n.eval κ) d)
      (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod (p : ℕ)),
      a ((PG).recInput κ p f x) = (PG).encRec κ p f x

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The target is exactly the conjunction of its displayed algorithm obligations.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem pgTargets_iff :
    PGTargets ℓ n d ↔
      (∃ a : List Bool → List Bool, PolyTimeComputable a ∧
        ∀ κ (p : ℕ+) (f : PolyTensor p (ℓ.eval κ) (n.eval κ) d),
          a ((PG).lgenInput κ p f) = (PG).encLgen κ p f) ∧
      (∃ a : List Bool → List Bool, PolyTimeComputable a ∧
        ∀ κ (p : ℕ+) (f : PolyTensor p (ℓ.eval κ) (n.eval κ) d)
          (x : Fin (ℓ.eval κ) → ZMod (p : ℕ)),
          a ((PG).recInput κ p f x) = (PG).encRec κ p f x)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The linear-time encryption input supplies the numeric dimensions, public group, key,
message and complete draw [GJLS21, Definition 4.6, printed p.22]. This is uniform input
layout glue; no dimension, modulus, key or randomness is hard-wired in the machine.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def linearEncInput (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n d κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ)
    (pk : Quadratic.MPK G (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) (PolyExpr.const n) κ pp)
    (x : Fin ((phfeClass (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) G.wG d).pubLen.eval κ) → Bool)
    (y : Fin ((phfeClass (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) G.wG d).privLen.eval κ) → Bool)
    (ω : Quadratic.EncDraw G κ pp) : List Bool :=
  NUPPT.advInput κ
    (pairEncode (Candidates.natToList (Nat.size ℓ) ℓ)
      (pairEncode (Candidates.natToList (Nat.size n) n)
        (pairEncode pp.encode
          (pairEncode (List.ofFn (encMPK G (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) κ pp pk))
            (pairEncode (List.ofFn x)
              (pairEncode (List.ofFn y) (Wire.quadraticEncDraw pp ω)))))))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The encryption layout exposes both dimensions and every deterministic core input.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem linearEncInput_eq (G : BilinearGen) (ℓ n d κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ)
    (pk : Quadratic.MPK G (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) (PolyExpr.const n) κ pp)
    (x : Fin ((phfeClass (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) G.wG d).pubLen.eval κ) → Bool)
    (y : Fin ((phfeClass (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) G.wG d).privLen.eval κ) → Bool)
    (ω : Quadratic.EncDraw G κ pp) :
    linearEncInput G ℓ n d κ pp pk x y ω = NUPPT.advInput κ
      (pairEncode (Candidates.natToList (Nat.size ℓ) ℓ)
        (pairEncode (Candidates.natToList (Nat.size n) n)
          (pairEncode pp.encode
            (pairEncode (List.ofFn (encMPK G (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) κ pp pk))
              (pairEncode (List.ofFn x)
                (pairEncode (List.ofFn y) (Wire.quadraticEncDraw pp ω)))))))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
One finite Turing machine encrypts in `(ℓ+n)q(κ)` steps uniformly in the numeric
message dimensions, degree and security parameter [GJLS21, Definition 4.6, printed p.22].
Phase B obligation; not proved in this development.

The target strengthens the source's circuit/supported-key formulation to one uniform
machine and all typed keys. The positive-size domain is explicit: the raw algorithms
remain total at zero size, while the source's multiplicative bound presumes nonempty
messages. The scalar word width is absorbed into the one polynomial `q`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def LinearEfficient (G : BilinearGen) : Prop :=
  ∃ M : FinTM Bool, ∃ q : PolyExpr, ∀ (ℓ n d κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ)
    (pk : Quadratic.MPK G (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) (PolyExpr.const n) κ pp)
    (x : Fin ((phfeClass (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) G.wG d).pubLen.eval κ) → Bool)
    (y : Fin ((phfeClass (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) G.wG d).privLen.eval κ) → Bool)
    (ω : Quadratic.EncDraw G κ pp), 0 < ℓ + n →
    M.ComputesInTime (PHFE.linearEncInput G ℓ n d κ pp pk x y ω)
      (List.ofFn (PHFE.encCT G (PolyExpr.const n) κ pp
        (PHFE.encCore G (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) d κ pp pk x y ω))) ((ℓ + n) * q.eval
          κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Linear efficiency chooses its one machine and polynomial before every numeric size.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem linearEfficient_iff (G : BilinearGen) : LinearEfficient G ↔
    ∃ M : FinTM Bool, ∃ q : PolyExpr, ∀ (ℓ n d κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ)
      (pk : Quadratic.MPK G (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) (PolyExpr.const n) κ pp)
      (x : Fin ((phfeClass (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) G.wG d).pubLen.eval κ) → Bool)
      (y : Fin ((phfeClass (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) G.wG d).privLen.eval κ) → Bool)
      (ω : Quadratic.EncDraw G κ pp), 0 < ℓ + n →
      M.ComputesInTime (PHFE.linearEncInput G ℓ n d κ pp pk x y ω)
        (List.ofFn (PHFE.encCT G (PolyExpr.const n) κ pp
          (PHFE.encCore G (PolyExpr.const ℓ) (PolyExpr.const n) d κ pp pk x y ω))) ((ℓ + n) * q.eval
            κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Uniform preprocessing computes the explicit MDDH hybrid from its scalar advice and
canonical DLIN challenge [Wee20, Section 2.1, p.4, polynomial-loss implementation].
Phase B obligation; not proved in this development.

The witness is chosen before κ, every advice value and every challenge. The fixed prime
schedule only indexes scalar advice; the modulus is read from the challenge. This is an
L1 preprocessing target, distinct from the L2 interactive-realiser hypotheses.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def MddhPreTargets (G : BilinearGen) : Prop :=
  ∀ (p : ℕ → ℕ) (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (_D : NUPPT),
    ∃ f : List Bool → List Bool, PolyTimeComputable f ∧
      ∀ κ (ω : BilinearGen.MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ) (c : G.DLINChallenge κ),
        f (pairEncode (G.mddhAdviceEnc p hp d ℓ κ ω) (G.dlinEnc κ c)) =
          G.mddhPre p hp d ℓ κ ω c

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The preprocessing target is one polynomial-time map before all advice/challenge pairs.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem mddhPreTargets_iff (G : BilinearGen) : MddhPreTargets G ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ → ℕ) (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (_D : NUPPT),
      ∃ f : List Bool → List Bool, PolyTimeComputable f ∧
        ∀ κ (ω : BilinearGen.MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ) (c : G.DLINChallenge κ),
          f (pairEncode (G.mddhAdviceEnc p hp d ℓ κ ω) (G.dlinEnc κ c)) =
            G.mddhPre p hp d ℓ κ ω c

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The uniform L1 preprocessing target supplies machine realisers for every fixed advice
family by the shared realisation theorem [Wee20, Section 2.1, p.4]. Realisers are constrained
only on encoded challenges and layout-length coins. No sampler or reduction machine is
constructed locally.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem mddhRealizable_of_preTarget (G : BilinearGen) (hT : MddhPreTargets G)
    (p : ℕ → ℕ) (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (d ℓ : PolyExpr) :
    G.MDDHRealizable p hp d ℓ

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
The five honest-algorithm fields are the exact efficient-interface obligations for the
concrete layered PHFE construction [GJLS21, Definition 4.1; Wee20, Section 3.1].
Phase B obligation; not proved in this development.

The public-generation target covers the nonidentity-generator draw after the already
uniform description generator. Every sampler target uses one complete draw type.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
structure SchemeTargets : Prop where
  /-- Uniformly draw the nonidentity public generator after the group description. -/
  pubGen_eff : SamplesEfficiently
    (fun κ (g : GroupDescription (S).G κ) => g.val)
    (fun κ g (r : GeneratorDraw (S).G κ g) => List.ofFn (((S).G.group κ g.val).encG r.val))
    (fun κ _ (pp : PublicParams (S).G κ) => pp.encode) (publicParamsCore (S).G)
  /-- Uniformly sample the complete honest setup draw and encode both keys. -/
  setup_eff : SamplesEfficiently
    (fun κ (pp : PublicParams (S).G κ) => pp.encode) (S).encSetupDraw
    (fun κ pp (o : (S).MPK κ pp × (S).MSK κ pp) =>
      pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encMPK κ pp o.1)) (List.ofFn ((S).encMSK κ pp o.2))) (S).setupCore
  /-- Uniformly sample encryption with pp, the public key, and both inputs supplied. -/
  enc_eff : SamplesEfficiently
    (fun κ (π : Σ pp : PublicParams (S).G κ,
        (S).MPK κ pp × (Fin ((C).pubLen.eval κ) → Bool) × (Fin ((C).privLen.eval κ) → Bool)) =>
      pairEncode π.1.encode (pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encMPK κ π.1 π.2.1))
        (pairEncode (List.ofFn π.2.2.1) (List.ofFn π.2.2.2))))
    (fun κ π => (S).encEncDraw κ π.1 π.2.1 π.2.2.1 π.2.2.2)
    (fun κ π (o : (S).CT κ π.1) => List.ofFn ((S).encCT κ π.1 o))
    (fun κ π => (S).encCore κ π.1 π.2.1 π.2.2.1 π.2.2.2)
  /-- Uniformly sample a function key with pp, the master key, and function supplied. -/
  keyGen_eff : SamplesEfficiently
    (fun κ (π : Σ pp : PublicParams (S).G κ, (S).MSK κ pp × (Fin ((C).fnLen.eval κ) → Bool)) =>
      pairEncode π.1.encode
        (pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encMSK κ π.1 π.2.1)) (List.ofFn π.2.2)))
    (fun κ π => (S).encKeyDraw κ π.1 π.2.1 π.2.2)
    (fun κ π (o : (S).SK κ π.1) => List.ofFn ((S).encSK κ π.1 o))
    (fun κ π => (S).keyCore κ π.1 π.2.1 π.2.2)
  /-- One polynomial-time map computes deterministic decryption at every public group. -/
  dec_eff : ∃ a : List Bool → List Bool, PolyTimeComputable a ∧
    ∀ κ (pp : PublicParams (S).G κ) (sk : (S).SK κ pp)
      (x : Fin ((C).pubLen.eval κ) → Bool) (ct : (S).CT κ pp),
      a (NUPPT.advInput κ (pairEncode pp.encode
        (pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encSK κ pp sk))
          (pairEncode (List.ofFn x) (List.ofFn ((S).encCT κ pp ct)))))) =
        match (S).dec κ pp sk x ct with
        | none => [false]
        | some o => true :: List.ofFn ((S).encDecOut κ pp o)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The target is exactly the conjunction of its displayed algorithm obligations.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem schemeTargets_iff :
    SchemeTargets G ℓ n d ↔
      (SamplesEfficiently
        (fun κ (g : GroupDescription (S).G κ) => g.val)
        (fun κ g (r : GeneratorDraw (S).G κ g) => List.ofFn (((S).G.group κ g.val).encG r.val))
        (fun κ _ (pp : PublicParams (S).G κ) => pp.encode) (publicParamsCore (S).G)) ∧
      (SamplesEfficiently
        (fun κ (pp : PublicParams (S).G κ) => pp.encode) (S).encSetupDraw
        (fun κ pp (o : (S).MPK κ pp × (S).MSK κ pp) =>
          pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encMPK κ pp o.1)) (List.ofFn ((S).encMSK κ pp o.2)))
            (S).setupCore) ∧
      (SamplesEfficiently
        (fun κ (π : Σ pp : PublicParams (S).G κ,
            (S).MPK κ pp × (Fin ((C).pubLen.eval κ) → Bool) × (Fin ((C).privLen.eval κ) → Bool)) =>
          pairEncode π.1.encode (pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encMPK κ π.1 π.2.1))
            (pairEncode (List.ofFn π.2.2.1) (List.ofFn π.2.2.2))))
        (fun κ π => (S).encEncDraw κ π.1 π.2.1 π.2.2.1 π.2.2.2)
        (fun κ π (o : (S).CT κ π.1) => List.ofFn ((S).encCT κ π.1 o))
        (fun κ π => (S).encCore κ π.1 π.2.1 π.2.2.1 π.2.2.2)) ∧
      (SamplesEfficiently
        (fun κ (π : Σ pp : PublicParams (S).G κ, (S).MSK κ pp × (Fin ((C).fnLen.eval κ) → Bool)) =>
          pairEncode π.1.encode
            (pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encMSK κ π.1 π.2.1)) (List.ofFn π.2.2)))
        (fun κ π => (S).encKeyDraw κ π.1 π.2.1 π.2.2)
        (fun κ π (o : (S).SK κ π.1) => List.ofFn ((S).encSK κ π.1 o))
        (fun κ π => (S).keyCore κ π.1 π.2.1 π.2.2)) ∧
      (∃ a : List Bool → List Bool, PolyTimeComputable a ∧
        ∀ κ (pp : PublicParams (S).G κ) (sk : (S).SK κ pp)
          (x : Fin ((C).pubLen.eval κ) → Bool) (ct : (S).CT κ pp),
          a (NUPPT.advInput κ (pairEncode pp.encode
            (pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encSK κ pp sk))
              (pairEncode (List.ofFn x) (List.ofFn ((S).encCT κ pp ct)))))) =
            match (S).dec κ pp sk x ct with
            | none => [false]
            | some o => true :: List.ofFn ((S).encDecOut κ pp o))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose:
Both concrete stateful simulators carry their own three shared sampler obligations
[GJLS21, Definition 4.3; Wee20, Section 2.2].
Phase B obligation; not proved in this development.

The committed targets include the full allowed information and its ordered index. They
are stated separately: no input-preprocessing or product-sampler closure is assumed.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
structure SimTargets : Prop where
  /-- The concrete committed simulator's setup draw and core satisfy the shared contract. -/
  sim_setup_eff : SamplesEfficiently
    (fun κ (pp : PublicParams (S).G κ) => pp.encode) (Sim).encSetupDraw
    (fun κ pp (o : (S).MPK κ pp × (Sim).St κ pp) =>
      pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encMPK κ pp o.1)) ((Sim).encSt κ pp o.2)) (Sim).setupCore
  /-- The concrete committed simulator's enc draw and core satisfy the shared contract. -/
  sim_enc_eff : SamplesEfficiently (Sim).encInputWord
    (fun κ π => (Sim).encEncDraw κ π.pp π.state π.omega)
    (fun κ π (o : (S).CT κ π.pp × (Sim).St κ π.pp) =>
      pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encCT κ π.pp o.1)) ((Sim).encSt κ π.pp o.2))
    (fun κ π => (Sim).encCore κ π.pp π.state π.omega)
  /-- The concrete committed simulator's key draw and core satisfy the shared contract. -/
  sim_key_eff : SamplesEfficiently (Sim).keyInputWord
    (fun κ π => (Sim).encKeyDraw κ π.pp π.state π.omega π.index)
    (fun κ π (o : (S).SK κ π.pp × (Sim).St κ π.pp) =>
      pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encSK κ π.pp o.1)) ((Sim).encSt κ π.pp o.2))
    (fun κ π => (Sim).keyCore κ π.pp π.state π.omega π.index)
  /-- The concrete semi-adaptive simulator's setup draw and core satisfy the shared contract. -/
  sa_setup_eff : SamplesEfficiently
    (fun κ (pp : PublicParams (S).G κ) => pp.encode) (SASim).encSetupDraw
    (fun κ pp (o : (S).MPK κ pp × (SASim).St κ pp) =>
      pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encMPK κ pp o.1)) ((SASim).encSt κ pp o.2)) (SASim).setupCore
  /-- The concrete semi-adaptive simulator's enc draw and core satisfy the shared contract. -/
  sa_enc_eff : SamplesEfficiently (SASim).encInputWord
    (fun κ π => (SASim).encEncDraw κ π.pp π.state π.publicInput)
    (fun κ π (o : (S).CT κ π.pp × (SASim).St κ π.pp) =>
      pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encCT κ π.pp o.1)) ((SASim).encSt κ π.pp o.2))
    (fun κ π => (SASim).encCore κ π.pp π.state π.publicInput)
  /-- The concrete semi-adaptive simulator's key draw and core satisfy the shared contract. -/
  sa_key_eff : SamplesEfficiently (SASim).keyInputWord
    (fun κ π => (SASim).encKeyDraw κ π.pp π.state π.publicInput π.function π.value)
    (fun κ π (o : (S).SK κ π.pp × (SASim).St κ π.pp) =>
      pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encSK κ π.pp o.1)) ((SASim).encSt κ π.pp o.2))
    (fun κ π => (SASim).keyCore κ π.pp π.state π.publicInput π.function π.value)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The target is exactly the conjunction of its displayed algorithm obligations.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem simTargets_iff :
    SimTargets G ℓ n d ↔
      (SamplesEfficiently
        (fun κ (pp : PublicParams (S).G κ) => pp.encode) (Sim).encSetupDraw
        (fun κ pp (o : (S).MPK κ pp × (Sim).St κ pp) =>
          pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encMPK κ pp o.1)) ((Sim).encSt κ pp o.2)) (Sim).setupCore) ∧
      (SamplesEfficiently (Sim).encInputWord
        (fun κ π => (Sim).encEncDraw κ π.pp π.state π.omega)
        (fun κ π (o : (S).CT κ π.pp × (Sim).St κ π.pp) =>
          pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encCT κ π.pp o.1)) ((Sim).encSt κ π.pp o.2))
        (fun κ π => (Sim).encCore κ π.pp π.state π.omega)) ∧
      (SamplesEfficiently (Sim).keyInputWord
        (fun κ π => (Sim).encKeyDraw κ π.pp π.state π.omega π.index)
        (fun κ π (o : (S).SK κ π.pp × (Sim).St κ π.pp) =>
          pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encSK κ π.pp o.1)) ((Sim).encSt κ π.pp o.2))
        (fun κ π => (Sim).keyCore κ π.pp π.state π.omega π.index)) ∧
      (SamplesEfficiently
        (fun κ (pp : PublicParams (S).G κ) => pp.encode) (SASim).encSetupDraw
        (fun κ pp (o : (S).MPK κ pp × (SASim).St κ pp) =>
          pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encMPK κ pp o.1)) ((SASim).encSt κ pp o.2)) (SASim).setupCore)
            ∧
      (SamplesEfficiently (SASim).encInputWord
        (fun κ π => (SASim).encEncDraw κ π.pp π.state π.publicInput)
        (fun κ π (o : (S).CT κ π.pp × (SASim).St κ π.pp) =>
          pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encCT κ π.pp o.1)) ((SASim).encSt κ π.pp o.2))
        (fun κ π => (SASim).encCore κ π.pp π.state π.publicInput)) ∧
      (SamplesEfficiently (SASim).keyInputWord
        (fun κ π => (SASim).encKeyDraw κ π.pp π.state π.publicInput π.function π.value)
        (fun κ π (o : (S).SK κ π.pp × (SASim).St κ π.pp) =>
          pairEncode (List.ofFn ((S).encSK κ π.pp o.1)) ((SASim).encSt κ π.pp o.2))
        (fun κ π => (SASim).keyCore κ π.pp π.state π.publicInput π.function π.value))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode a source-group vector in increasing coordinate order.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def groupVector {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → pp.group.G) : List Bool :=
  (List.ofFn fun i => List.ofFn (pp.group.encG (v i))).flatten

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The group-vector word concatenates its fixed-width element encodings.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem groupVector_eq {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → pp.group.G) :
    groupVector pp v = (List.ofFn fun i => List.ofFn (pp.group.encG (v i))).flatten

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode a source-group matrix in increasing row and column order.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def groupMatrix {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) pp.group.G) : List Bool :=
  (List.ofFn fun i => groupVector pp (A i)).flatten

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The matrix word is the concatenation of its group-vector row words.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem groupMatrix_eq {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) pp.group.G) :
    groupMatrix pp A = (List.ofFn fun i => groupVector pp (A i)).flatten

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode Π's public key in its four public matrix blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def linearMPK {ℓ z : PolyExpr} (pk : Linear.MPK G ℓ z κ pp) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (groupMatrix pp pk.A) (pairEncode (groupMatrix pp pk.AW)
    (pairEncode (groupMatrix pp (fun i j => pk.AU i (finProdFinEquiv.symm j)))
      (groupMatrix pp pk.AV)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The public-key word has exactly the four specified matrix blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem linearMPK_eq {ℓ z : PolyExpr} (pk : Linear.MPK G ℓ z κ pp) :
    linearMPK pp pk = pairEncode (groupMatrix pp pk.A) (pairEncode (groupMatrix pp pk.AW)
      (pairEncode (groupMatrix pp (fun i j => pk.AU i (finProdFinEquiv.symm j)))
        (groupMatrix pp pk.AV)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode Π's scalar master secret at the public source-group width.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def linearMSK {ℓ z : PolyExpr} (sk : Linear.MSK G ℓ z κ pp) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (G.wG.eval κ) sk.W)
    (pairEncode (Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (G.wG.eval κ)
      (fun i j => sk.U i (finProdFinEquiv.symm j)))
      (Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (G.wG.eval κ) sk.V))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The master-secret word is the displayed scalar matrix encoding.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem linearMSK_eq {ℓ z : PolyExpr} (sk : Linear.MSK G ℓ z κ pp) :
    linearMSK pp sk = pairEncode (Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (G.wG.eval κ) sk.W)
      (pairEncode (Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (G.wG.eval κ)
        (fun i j => sk.U i (finProdFinEquiv.symm j)))
        (Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (G.wG.eval κ) sk.V))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode Π's ciphertext by concatenating its three fixed-size group vectors.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def linearCT {z : PolyExpr} (ct : Linear.CT G z κ pp) : List Bool :=
  groupVector pp ct.c0 ++ groupVector pp ct.c1 ++ groupVector pp ct.c2

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The ciphertext word concatenates the three source-group blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem linearCT_eq {z : PolyExpr} (ct : Linear.CT G z κ pp) :
    linearCT pp ct = groupVector pp ct.c0 ++ groupVector pp ct.c1 ++
      groupVector pp ct.c2

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode a function key using the partial garbling's published node coordinates.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def linearKey {f : Fn κ pp.orderParam} (sk : Linear.Key G PG κ pp f) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (groupMatrix pp sk.K1)
    (pairEncode (groupMatrix pp (fun i j =>
      let a := finProdFinEquiv.symm j
      sk.K2 i (a.1, (PG.mCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm a.2)))
      (pairEncode (groupMatrix pp (fun i j => sk.K3 i ((PG.mCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j)))
        (groupMatrix pp (fun i j => sk.R i ((PG.mCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j)))))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The function-key word uses `K1,K2,K3,R` in that order.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem linearKey_eq {f : Fn κ pp.orderParam} (sk : Linear.Key G PG κ pp f) :
    linearKey pp PG sk = pairEncode (groupMatrix pp sk.K1)
      (pairEncode (groupMatrix pp (fun i j =>
        let a := finProdFinEquiv.symm j
        sk.K2 i (a.1, (PG.mCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm a.2)))
        (pairEncode (groupMatrix pp
          (fun i j => sk.K3 i ((PG.mCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j)))
          (groupMatrix pp (fun i j => sk.R i ((PG.mCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j)))))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode an outer public key by its two masks and Π's public key.
The outer public-key word is the displayed three-block pair.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem quadraticMPK_eq {ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr} (pk : Quadratic.MPK G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) :
    quadraticMPK pp pk = pairEncode (groupMatrix pp pk.A1)
      (pairEncode (groupMatrix pp pk.A2) (linearMPK pp pk.linear))

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode the outer master secret with its public matrix metadata.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def quadraticMSK {ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr} (sk : Quadratic.MSK G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (groupMatrix pp sk.matrix) (linearMSK pp sk.linear)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The outer master-secret word retains its public matrix and Π's secret word.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem quadraticMSK_eq {ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr} (sk : Quadratic.MSK G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) :
    quadraticMSK pp sk = pairEncode (groupMatrix pp sk.matrix) (linearMSK pp sk.linear)

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode the outer ciphertext by the two masks followed by Π's ciphertext.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def quadraticCT {n1 n2 : PolyExpr} (ct : Quadratic.CT G n1 n2 κ pp) : List Bool :=
  groupVector pp ct.y1 ++ groupVector pp ct.y2 ++ linearCT pp ct.linear

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The outer ciphertext word is the displayed concatenation.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem quadraticCT_eq {n1 n2 : PolyExpr} (ct : Quadratic.CT G n1 n2 κ pp) :
    quadraticCT pp ct = groupVector pp ct.y1 ++ groupVector pp ct.y2 ++
      linearCT pp ct.linear

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode an outer key by its public matrix and Π's key.
The outer key word is the displayed public-matrix and linear-key pair.
Encode all scalar vector coordinates at the public source-group width.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def scalarVector {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → ZMod pp.group.order) : List Bool :=
  Encoding.Modular.encodeVector (G.wG.eval κ) v

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The word retains exactly the displayed complete coordinate blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem scalarVector_eq {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → ZMod pp.group.order) :
    scalarVector pp v =
      Encoding.Modular.encodeVector (G.wG.eval κ) v

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode all scalar matrix coordinates using the shared modular matrix representation.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def scalarMatrix {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) (ZMod pp.group.order)) : List Bool :=
  Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (G.wG.eval κ) A

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The word retains exactly the displayed complete coordinate blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem scalarMatrix_eq {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) (ZMod pp.group.order)) :
    scalarMatrix pp A =
      Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (G.wG.eval κ) A

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode all four scalar blocks of a linear setup draw.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def linearSetupDraw {ℓ z : PolyExpr} (ω : Linear.SetupDraw G ℓ z κ pp) : List Bool :=
  [scalarMatrix pp ω.1, scalarMatrix pp ω.2.1,
    scalarMatrix pp (fun i j => ω.2.2.1 i (finProdFinEquiv.symm j)),
    scalarMatrix pp ω.2.2.2].foldr pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The word retains exactly the displayed complete coordinate blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem linearSetupDraw_eq {ℓ z : PolyExpr} (ω : Linear.SetupDraw G ℓ z κ pp) :
    linearSetupDraw pp ω =
      [scalarMatrix pp ω.1, scalarMatrix pp ω.2.1,
        scalarMatrix pp (fun i j => ω.2.2.1 i (finProdFinEquiv.symm j)),
        scalarMatrix pp ω.2.2.2].foldr pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode the outer masks and the complete linear setup draw.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def quadraticSetupDraw {ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr}
    (ω : Quadratic.SetupDraw G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) : List Bool :=
  [scalarMatrix pp ω.1, scalarMatrix pp ω.2.1,
    linearSetupDraw pp ω.2.2].foldr pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The word retains exactly the displayed complete coordinate blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem quadraticSetupDraw_eq {ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr}
    (ω : Quadratic.SetupDraw G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) :
    quadraticSetupDraw pp ω =
      [scalarMatrix pp ω.1, scalarMatrix pp ω.2.1,
        linearSetupDraw pp ω.2.2].foldr pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode all six scalar coordinates of an outer encryption draw.
The word retains exactly the displayed complete coordinate blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem quadraticEncDraw_eq (ω : Quadratic.EncDraw G κ pp) :
    quadraticEncDraw pp ω =
      [scalarVector pp ω.1, scalarVector pp ω.2.1,
        scalarVector pp ω.2.2].foldr pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode the complete function-dependent T and R draw in its supplied coordinates.
The word retains exactly the displayed complete coordinate blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem linearKeyDraw_eq {ℓ n' : PolyExpr} {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type}
    (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ n' Fn) {f : Fn κ pp.orderParam}
    (ω : Linear.KeyDraw G PG κ pp f) :
    linearKeyDraw pp PG ω =
      [scalarMatrix pp (fun i j => ω.1 i ((PG.rowCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j)),
        scalarMatrix pp (fun i j => ω.2 i ((PG.mCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j))].foldr
        pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode all seven independent scalar blocks of a linear simulator setup draw.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def linearSimSetupDraw {ℓ z : PolyExpr}
    (ω : Linear.SimSetupDraw G ℓ z κ pp) : List Bool :=
  [scalarMatrix pp ω.1, scalarVector pp ω.2.1, scalarMatrix pp ω.2.2.1,
    scalarMatrix pp (fun i j => ω.2.2.2.1 i (finProdFinEquiv.symm j)),
    scalarMatrix pp ω.2.2.2.2.1, scalarVector pp ω.2.2.2.2.2.1,
    scalarVector pp ω.2.2.2.2.2.2].foldr pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The word retains exactly the displayed complete coordinate blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem linearSimSetupDraw_eq {ℓ z : PolyExpr}
    (ω : Linear.SimSetupDraw G ℓ z κ pp) :
    linearSimSetupDraw pp ω =
      [scalarMatrix pp ω.1, scalarVector pp ω.2.1, scalarMatrix pp ω.2.2.1,
        scalarMatrix pp (fun i j => ω.2.2.2.1 i (finProdFinEquiv.symm j)),
        scalarMatrix pp ω.2.2.2.2.1, scalarVector pp ω.2.2.2.2.2.1,
        scalarVector pp ω.2.2.2.2.2.2].foldr pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode both outer masks and the complete linear simulator setup draw.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def quadraticSimSetupDraw {ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr}
    (ω : Quadratic.SimSetupDraw G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) : List Bool :=
  [scalarMatrix pp ω.1, scalarMatrix pp ω.2.1,
    linearSimSetupDraw pp ω.2.2].foldr pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The word retains exactly the displayed complete coordinate blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem quadraticSimSetupDraw_eq {ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr}
    (ω : Quadratic.SimSetupDraw G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) :
    quadraticSimSetupDraw pp ω =
      [scalarMatrix pp ω.1, scalarMatrix pp ω.2.1,
        linearSimSetupDraw pp ω.2.2].foldr pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode all four blocks of a linear key-simulation draw.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def linearSimKeyDraw {ℓ n' : PolyExpr} {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type}
    (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ n' Fn) {f : Fn κ pp.orderParam}
    (ω : Linear.SimKeyDraw G PG κ pp f) : List Bool :=
  [scalarMatrix pp (fun i j => ω.1 i ((PG.rowCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j)),
    scalarVector pp (fun j => ω.2.1 ((PG.l1ColCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j)),
    scalarMatrix pp (fun i j => ω.2.2.1 i ((PG.mCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j)),
    scalarVector pp (fun j => ω.2.2.2 ((PG.rowCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j))].foldr
    pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The word retains exactly the displayed complete coordinate blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem linearSimKeyDraw_eq {ℓ n' : PolyExpr} {Fn : ℕ → ℕ+ → Type}
    (PG : PartialGarbling.Raw ℓ n' Fn) {f : Fn κ pp.orderParam}
    (ω : Linear.SimKeyDraw G PG κ pp f) :
    linearSimKeyDraw pp PG ω =
      [scalarMatrix pp (fun i j => ω.1 i ((PG.rowCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j)),
        scalarVector pp (fun j => ω.2.1 ((PG.l1ColCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j)),
        scalarMatrix pp (fun i j => ω.2.2.1 i ((PG.mCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j)),
        scalarVector pp (fun j => ω.2.2.2 ((PG.rowCoord κ pp.orderParam f).symm j))].foldr
        pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode every scalar field of the linear simulator state, including the total inverse.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def linearSimState {ℓ z : PolyExpr} (st : Linear.SimState G ℓ z κ pp) : List Bool :=
  [scalarMatrix pp st.A, scalarMatrix pp st.W,
    scalarMatrix pp (fun i j => st.U i (finProdFinEquiv.symm j)), scalarMatrix pp st.V,
    scalarVector pp st.c, scalarVector pp st.w, scalarVector pp st.v,
    scalarMatrix pp st.basisInv].foldr pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The word retains exactly the displayed complete coordinate blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem linearSimState_eq {ℓ z : PolyExpr} (st : Linear.SimState G ℓ z κ pp) :
    linearSimState pp st =
      [scalarMatrix pp st.A, scalarMatrix pp st.W,
        scalarMatrix pp (fun i j => st.U i (finProdFinEquiv.symm j)), scalarMatrix pp st.V,
        scalarVector pp st.c, scalarVector pp st.w, scalarVector pp st.v,
        scalarMatrix pp st.basisInv].foldr pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: Encode the outer matrix, complete linear state and both retained scalar masks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
def quadraticSimState {ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr}
    (st : Quadratic.SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) : List Bool :=
  [groupMatrix pp st.matrix, linearSimState pp st.linear,
    scalarVector pp st.y1, scalarVector pp st.y2].foldr pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.prose: The word retains exactly the displayed complete coordinate blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.AdvancedEncryption.F.header:
theorem quadraticSimState_eq {ℓ n1 n2 : PolyExpr}
    (st : Quadratic.SimState G ℓ n1 n2 κ pp) :
    quadraticSimState pp st =
      [groupMatrix pp st.matrix, linearSimState pp st.linear,
        scalarVector pp st.y1, scalarVector pp st.y2].foldr pairEncode []

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupDot.prose:
Multiply group entries raised to the known scalar coordinates. This is technical glue
for the implicit matrix arithmetic of [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupDot.header:
def groupDot [Fintype ι] (v : ι → H) (a : ι → ZMod p) : H :=
  ∏ i, v i ^ (a i).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupDot_eq.prose: `groupDot v a` is the product of the powers `v i ^ (a i).val`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupDot_eq.header:
theorem groupDot_eq [Fintype ι] (v : ι → H) (a : ι → ZMod p) :
    groupDot v a = ∏ i, v i ^ (a i).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupMulVec.prose:
Multiply a group-valued matrix by a known scalar column vector using group operations.
This is the implicit representation of matrix action [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupMulVec.header:
def groupMulVec [Fintype κ] (M : Matrix ι κ H) (a : κ → ZMod p) : ι → H :=
  fun i => groupDot (M i) a

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupMulVec_.prose: Each coordinate of `groupMulVec M a` is the product of one row's known powers.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupMulVec_.header:
theorem groupMulVec_apply [Fintype κ] (M : Matrix ι κ H) (a : κ → ZMod p) (i : ι) :
    groupMulVec M a i = groupDot (M i) a

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupVecMul.prose:
Multiply a known scalar row vector by a group-valued matrix using group operations.
This follows the row-vector convention of [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupVecMul.header:
def groupVecMul [Fintype ι] (a : ι → ZMod p) (M : Matrix ι κ H) : κ → H :=
  fun j => groupDot (fun i => M i j) a

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupVecMul_.prose: Each coordinate of `groupVecMul a M` is the product of one column's known powers.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupVecMul_.header:
theorem groupVecMul_apply [Fintype ι] (a : ι → ZMod p) (M : Matrix ι κ H) (j : κ) :
    groupVecMul a M j = groupDot (fun i => M i j) a

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupMatMul.prose:
Multiply a group-valued matrix on the right by a known scalar matrix, using products and
powers only [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4; §4.2, p. 9].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupMatMul.header:
def groupMatMul [Fintype κ] (M : Matrix ι κ H) (N : Matrix κ υ (ZMod p)) :
    Matrix ι υ H := fun i j => groupDot (M i) (fun k => N k j)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupMatMul_.prose: An entry of `groupMatMul M N` is the product of powers along the shared index.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupMatMul_.header:
theorem groupMatMul_apply [Fintype κ] (M : Matrix ι κ H) (N : Matrix κ υ (ZMod p))
    (i : ι) (j : υ) :
    groupMatMul M N i j = groupDot (M i) (fun k => N k j)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.matMulGroup.prose:
Multiply a group-valued matrix on the left by a known scalar matrix, using products and
powers only [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4; §4.2, p. 10, (12)].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.matMulGroup.header:
def matMulGroup [Fintype κ] (M : Matrix ι κ (ZMod p)) (N : Matrix κ υ H) :
    Matrix ι υ H := fun i j => groupDot (fun k => N k j) (M i)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.matMulGroup_.prose: An entry of `matMulGroup M N` is the product of the known powers in a column of `N`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.matMulGroup_.header:
theorem matMulGroup_apply [Fintype κ] (M : Matrix ι κ (ZMod p)) (N : Matrix κ υ H)
    (i : ι) (j : υ) :
    matMulGroup M N i j = groupDot (fun k => N k j) (M i)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
A source-group vector represents its scalar coordinates as powers of `g`
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header: def expVec (g : B.G) (a : ι → ZMod B.order) : ι → B.G := fun i => g ^ (a i).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose: A coordinate of the implicit vector is its scalar coordinate exponentiated at `g`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expVec_apply (g : B.G) (a : ι → ZMod B.order) (i : ι) :
    B.expVec g a i = g ^ (a i).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
A source-group matrix represents its scalar entries as powers of `g`
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
def expMat (g : B.G) (M : Matrix ι κ (ZMod B.order)) : Matrix ι κ B.G :=
  fun i j => g ^ (M i j).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose: An entry of the implicit matrix is its scalar entry exponentiated at `g`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expMat_apply (g : B.G) (M : Matrix ι κ (ZMod B.order)) (i : ι) (j : κ) :
    B.expMat g M i j = g ^ (M i j).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
A target-group vector represents its scalar coordinates as powers of `gT`
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
def expVecT (gT : B.GT) (a : ι → ZMod B.order) : ι → B.GT :=
  fun i => gT ^ (a i).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose: A coordinate of the target-group vector is its scalar coordinate raised at `gT`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expVecT_apply (gT : B.GT) (a : ι → ZMod B.order) (i : ι) :
    B.expVecT gT a i = gT ^ (a i).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
A target-group matrix represents its scalar entries as powers of `gT`
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
def expMatT (gT : B.GT) (M : Matrix ι κ (ZMod B.order)) : Matrix ι κ B.GT :=
  fun i j => gT ^ (M i j).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose: An entry of the target-group matrix is its scalar entry exponentiated at `gT`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expMatT_apply (gT : B.GT) (M : Matrix ι κ (ZMod B.order)) (i : ι) (j : κ) :
    B.expMatT gT M i j = gT ^ (M i j).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Pair corresponding vector entries and multiply in the target group, implementing the
implicit dot product [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4; §4.2, p. 9, (6)–(8)].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header: def pairVec [Fintype ι] (a b : ι → B.G) : B.GT := ∏ i, B.pair (a i) (b i)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose: The vector pairing is the product of the coordinate pairings.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem pairVec_eq [Fintype ι] (a b : ι → B.G) :
    B.pairVec a b = ∏ i, B.pair (a i) (b i)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Pair matrix rows against columns and multiply the pairings, implementing matrix
multiplication in the exponent [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4; §4.2, p. 9, (6)–(7)].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
def pairMat [Fintype κ] (M : Matrix ι κ B.G) (N : Matrix κ υ B.G) : Matrix ι υ B.GT :=
  fun i j => B.pairVec (M i) (fun k => N k j)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose: Each entry of the matrix pairing is a row-column vector pairing.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem pairMat_apply [Fintype κ] (M : Matrix ι κ B.G) (N : Matrix κ υ B.G)
    (i : ι) (j : υ) :
    B.pairMat M N i j = B.pairVec (M i) (fun k => N k j)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Pair all coordinate pairs of two source-group vectors. This supplies the target-group
representation of their scalar tensor product [Wee20, §3.1, p. 6].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
def pairTensor (a : ι → B.G) (b : κ → B.G) : ι × κ → B.GT :=
  fun ij => B.pair (a ij.1) (b ij.2)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose: A tensor-pairing coordinate is the pairing of its two indexed source-group entries.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem pairTensor_apply (a : ι → B.G) (b : κ → B.G) (ij : ι × κ) :
    B.pairTensor a b ij = B.pair (a ij.1) (b ij.2)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Target-group exponents add modulo the group order. Technical glue parallel to
`BilinearGroup.pow_val_add` for the source group; no target-group version is in that API.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem pow_val_add_GT (gT : B.GT) (a b : ZMod B.order) :
    gT ^ (a + b).val = gT ^ a.val * gT ^ b.val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Negating a target-group exponent inverts the group element. Technical glue parallel to
`BilinearGroup.pow_val_neg` for the source group.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem pow_val_neg_GT (gT : B.GT) (a : ZMod B.order) :
    gT ^ (-a).val = (gT ^ a.val)⁻¹

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Adding scalar vectors multiplies their implicit source-group vectors
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expVec_add (g : B.G) (a b : ι → ZMod B.order) :
    B.expVec g (a + b) = B.expVec g a * B.expVec g b

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Negating a scalar vector inverts its implicit source-group vector
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expVec_neg (g : B.G) (a : ι → ZMod B.order) :
    B.expVec g (-a) = (B.expVec g a)⁻¹

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Scalar multiplication acts on the implicit vector by known powers
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expVec_smul (g : B.G) (c : ZMod B.order) (a : ι → ZMod B.order) :
    B.expVec g (c • a) = fun i => (B.expVec g a i) ^ c.val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Adding scalar vectors multiplies their target-group representations
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expVecT_add (gT : B.GT) (a b : ι → ZMod B.order) :
    B.expVecT gT (a + b) = B.expVecT gT a * B.expVecT gT b

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Negating scalar coordinates inverts the target-group representation
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expVecT_neg (gT : B.GT) (a : ι → ZMod B.order) :
    B.expVecT gT (-a) = (B.expVecT gT a)⁻¹

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
A known scalar multiplies target-group exponents through known powers
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
