theorem expVecT_smul (gT : B.GT) (c : ZMod B.order) (a : ι → ZMod B.order) :
    B.expVecT gT (c • a) = fun i => (B.expVecT gT a i) ^ c.val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
An implicit scalar dot product is a product of known powers of source-group elements
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4; §4.2, p. 9, (8)].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem groupDot_expVec [Fintype ι] (g : B.G) (a b : ι → ZMod B.order) :
    groupDot (B.expVec g a) b = g ^ (dotProduct a b).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
A target-group scalar dot product is a product of known powers
[Wee20, §4.2, p. 9, (8)].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem groupDot_expVecT [Fintype ι] (gT : B.GT) (a b : ι → ZMod B.order) :
    groupDot (B.expVecT gT a) b = gT ^ (dotProduct a b).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
A known column-vector action commutes with the source-group implicit representation
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expMat_mulVec [Fintype κ] (g : B.G) (M : Matrix ι κ (ZMod B.order))
    (a : κ → ZMod B.order) :
    groupMulVec (B.expMat g M) a = B.expVec g (M *ᵥ a)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
A known row-vector action commutes with the source-group implicit representation
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expVec_vecMul [Fintype ι] (g : B.G) (a : ι → ZMod B.order)
    (M : Matrix ι κ (ZMod B.order)) :
    groupVecMul a (B.expMat g M) = B.expVec g (a ᵥ* M)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
A scalar matrix on the right can be applied to a group-valued implicit matrix
[Wee20, §4.2, p. 9, KeyGen].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expMat_mul [Fintype κ] (g : B.G) (M : Matrix ι κ (ZMod B.order))
    (N : Matrix κ υ (ZMod B.order)) :
    groupMatMul (B.expMat g M) N = B.expMat g (M * N)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
A scalar matrix on the left can be applied to a group-valued implicit matrix
[Wee20, §4.2, p. 10, (12)].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expMat_mul_left [Fintype κ] (g : B.G) (M : Matrix ι κ (ZMod B.order))
    (N : Matrix κ υ (ZMod B.order)) :
    matMulGroup M (B.expMat g N) = B.expMat g (M * N)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Known powers also implement a target-group matrix-vector action
[Wee20, §4.2, p. 9, (8)].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expMatT_mulVec [Fintype κ] (gT : B.GT) (M : Matrix ι κ (ZMod B.order))
    (a : κ → ZMod B.order) :
    groupMulVec (B.expMatT gT M) a = B.expVecT gT (M *ᵥ a)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Pairing corresponding implicit coordinates evaluates their scalar dot product
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4; §4.2, p. 9, (6)–(8)].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem pair_expVec [Fintype ι] (g h : B.G) (a b : ι → ZMod B.order) :
    B.pairVec (B.expVec g a) (B.expVec h b) = B.pair g h ^ (dotProduct a b).val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Pairing implicit rows and columns evaluates the scalar matrix product
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4; §4.2, p. 9, (6)–(7)].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem pair_expMat [Fintype κ] (g h : B.G) (M : Matrix ι κ (ZMod B.order))
    (N : Matrix κ υ (ZMod B.order)) :
    B.pairMat (B.expMat g M) (B.expMat h N) = B.expMatT (B.pair g h) (M * N)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Tensor pairings expose the product of their scalar coordinates in the target group
[Wee20, §3.1, p. 6].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem pairTensor_expVec (g h : B.G) (a : ι → ZMod B.order) (b : κ → ZMod B.order) :
    B.pairTensor (B.expVec g a) (B.expVec h b) =
      B.expVecT (B.pair g h) (fun ij : ι × κ => a ij.1 * b ij.2)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
A tensor product with its right scalar factor known is computable in the source group
[Wee20, §3.3, p. 8, Game 3].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expVec_tensor_left (g : B.G) (a : ι → ZMod B.order) (b : κ → ZMod B.order) :
    (fun ij : ι × κ => B.expVec g a ij.1 ^ (b ij.2).val) =
      B.expVec g (fun ij : ι × κ => a ij.1 * b ij.2)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
A tensor product with its left scalar factor known is computable in the source group
[Wee20, §3.3, p. 8, Game 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem expVec_tensor_right (g : B.G) (a : ι → ZMod B.order) (b : κ → ZMod B.order) :
    (fun ij : ι × κ => B.expVec g b ij.2 ^ (a ij.1).val) =
      B.expVec g (fun ij : ι × κ => a ij.1 * b ij.2)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.dlinStr.prose:
Serialize a public DLIN tuple as the description followed by the generator and five
source-group points [JLS26, §1.1, p. 3]. The generator is explicit because it is randomized
in the library convention; the paper's generator is canonical.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.dlinStr.header:
def dlinStr {wG wT : ℕ} (B : BilinearGroup wG wT) (d : List Bool)
    (g a b u v w : B.G) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode d (pairEncode (List.ofFn (B.encG g))
    (pairEncode (List.ofFn (B.encG a)) (pairEncode (List.ofFn (B.encG b))
      (pairEncode (List.ofFn (B.encG u))
        (pairEncode (List.ofFn (B.encG v)) (List.ofFn (B.encG w)))))))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.dlinStr_eq.prose: The DLIN input is the nested pair of the description and the six encoded group points.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.dlinStr_eq.header:
theorem dlinStr_eq {wG wT : ℕ} (B : BilinearGroup wG wT) (d : List Bool)
    (g a b u v w : B.G) :
    dlinStr B d g a b u v w =
      pairEncode d (pairEncode (List.ofFn (B.encG g))
        (pairEncode (List.ofFn (B.encG a)) (pairEncode (List.ofFn (B.encG b))
          (pairEncode (List.ofFn (B.encG u))
            (pairEncode (List.ofFn (B.encG v)) (List.ofFn (B.encG w)))))))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.length_dlinS.prose:
Fixed-width group encodings make the tuple length depend only on the description length
and group width. This is serialization glue for [JLS26, §1.1, p. 3].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.length_dlinS.header:
theorem length_dlinStr {wG wT : ℕ} (B : BilinearGroup wG wT) (d : List Bool)
    (g a b u v w : B.G) :
    (dlinStr B d g a b u v w).length = 2 * d.length + 11 * wG + 12

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.dlinMatrix.prose:
The DLIN matrix has rows `(a,0)`, `(0,b)`, and `(1,1)`
[GJLS21, §3, p. 17, the distribution preceding Definition 3.3].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.dlinMatrix.header:
def dlinMatrix {p : ℕ} (a b : ZMod p) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 2) (ZMod p) :=
  ![![a, 0], ![0, b], ![1, 1]]

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.dlinMatrix_e.prose: The three rows of the scalar DLIN matrix are its displayed definition.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.dlinMatrix_e.header:
theorem dlinMatrix_eq {p : ℕ} (a b : ZMod p) :
    dlinMatrix a b = ![![a, 0], ![0, b], ![1, 1]]

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.dlinMatrix_m.prose:
The real DLIN vector is the DLIN matrix applied to its two random scalars
[GJLS21, Definition 3.3, p. 18; JLS26, §1.1, p. 3].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.dlinMatrix_m.header:
theorem dlinMatrix_mulVec {p : ℕ} (a b r s : ZMod p) :
    dlinMatrix a b *ᵥ ![r, s] = ![a * r, b * s, r + s]

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
A reachable public DLIN challenge consists of shared public parameters and five
source-group points [JLS26, §1.1, p. 3]. The public parameters contain the actual reachable
description and a nonidentity generator, independently of any coins producing them.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
structure DLINChallenge (κ : ℕ) where
  /-- The shared group description and nonidentity generator. -/
  pp : PublicParams G κ
  /-- The first base power `g^a`. -/
  baseA : (G.group κ pp.description.val).G
  /-- The second base power `g^b`. -/
  baseB : (G.group κ pp.description.val).G
  /-- The first response coordinate. -/
  responseA : (G.group κ pp.description.val).G
  /-- The second response coordinate. -/
  responseB : (G.group κ pp.description.val).G
  /-- The last response coordinate. -/
  responseSum : (G.group κ pp.description.val).G

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Attach five group points to the shared public parameters. This is technical glue for
the sampling experiment of [JLS26, §1.1, p. 3].
The constructor records exactly its public parameters and five group points.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinChallenge_eq (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ)
    (a b u v w : (G.group κ pp.description.val).G) :
    G.dlinChallenge κ pp a b u v w = ⟨pp, a, b, u, v, w⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Encode precisely the public description, generator and five response points
[JLS26, §1.1, p. 3]. No generator coins or private scalar witnesses are encoded.
A challenge encodes as its public DLIN tuple.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinEnc_eq (κ : ℕ) (c : G.DLINChallenge κ) :
    G.dlinEnc κ c =
      dlinStr (G.group κ c.pp.description.val) c.pp.description.val c.pp.generator
        c.baseA c.baseB c.responseA c.responseB c.responseSum

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Encoding a constructed challenge produces its public tuple. This is the interface
between the typed experiment and its string input.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinEnc_dlinChallenge (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ)
    (a b u v w : (G.group κ pp.description.val).G) :
    G.dlinEnc κ (G.dlinChallenge κ pp a b u v w) =
      dlinStr (G.group κ pp.description.val) pp.description.val pp.generator a b u v w

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Public challenge encoding is injective; in particular two generator coin strings yielding
one public description do not create distinct encoded objects. Serialization glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header: theorem dlinEnc_injective (κ : ℕ) : Function.Injective (G.dlinEnc κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
A reachable public DLIN challenge has one fixed polynomial encoding length.
Serialization glue for [JLS26, §1.1, p. 3].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem length_dlinEnc (κ : ℕ) (c : G.DLINChallenge κ) :
    (G.dlinEnc κ c).length = 2 * G.descLen.eval κ + 11 * G.wG.eval κ + 12

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Sample the canonical DLIN challenge: group coins first, a uniform nonidentity generator,
then `a,b`, `r,s`, and the final random scalar `t` [JLS26, §1.1, p. 3]. The real response is
`(g^(ar),g^(bs),g^(r+s))`; the random response replaces only its last coordinate by `g^t`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
noncomputable def dlinSample (real : Bool) (κ : ℕ) : ProbComp (G.DLINChallenge κ) :=
  (publicParamsGen G κ).bind fun pp =>
  (ProbComp.sample (Fin 2 → ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order)).bind fun ab =>
  (ProbComp.sample (Fin 2 → ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order)).bind fun rs =>
  (ProbComp.sample (ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order)).bind fun t =>
    .pure (G.dlinChallenge κ pp (pp.generator ^ (ab 0).val) (pp.generator ^ (ab 1).val)
      (pp.generator ^ (ab 0 * rs 0).val) (pp.generator ^ (ab 1 * rs 1).val)
      (pp.generator ^ (if real then rs 0 + rs 1 else t).val))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The canonical sampling law uses shared sequential public-parameter generation followed
by the displayed scalar draws.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinSample_eq (real : Bool) (κ : ℕ) :
    G.dlinSample real κ =
      (publicParamsGen G κ).bind fun pp =>
      (ProbComp.sample (Fin 2 → ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order)).bind fun ab =>
      (ProbComp.sample (Fin 2 → ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order)).bind fun rs =>
      (ProbComp.sample (ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order)).bind fun t =>
        .pure (G.dlinChallenge κ pp (pp.generator ^ (ab 0).val) (pp.generator ^ (ab 1).val)
          (pp.generator ^ (ab 0 * rs 0).val) (pp.generator ^ (ab 1 * rs 1).val)
          (pp.generator ^ (if real then rs 0 + rs 1 else t).val))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Run a non-uniform PPT distinguisher on a canonical DLIN challenge, using independent
machine coins [JLS26, §1.1, p. 3]. The machine receives the security parameter through the
library's `distinguisherL` activation.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
noncomputable def dlinGame (D : NUPPT) (real : Bool) (κ : ℕ) : ProbComp Bool :=
  (G.dlinSample real κ).bind fun c =>
  (ProbComp.sample (D.Coins κ)).bind fun r =>
    .pure (D.distinguisherL κ (G.dlinEnc κ c) r)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The DLIN experiment draws a typed challenge and the distinguisher's independent coins.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinGame_eq (D : NUPPT) (real : Bool) (κ : ℕ) :
    G.dlinGame D real κ =
      (G.dlinSample real κ).bind fun c =>
      (ProbComp.sample (D.Coins κ)).bind fun r =>
        .pure (D.distinguisherL κ (G.dlinEnc κ c) r)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The DLIN advantage is the absolute difference of the two acceptance probabilities
[JLS26, §1.1, p. 3].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
noncomputable def dlinAdv (D : NUPPT) (κ : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  advantage (G.dlinGame D false κ) (G.dlinGame D true κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The DLIN advantage uses the library's two-experiment convention.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinAdv_eq (D : NUPPT) (κ : ℕ) :
    G.dlinAdv D κ = advantage (G.dlinGame D false κ) (G.dlinGame D true κ)
def DLINAssumption : Prop := ∀ D : NUPPT, Negligible (G.dlinAdv D)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: DLIN hardness is negligibility of every non-uniform PPT advantage.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinAssumption_iff :
    G.DLINAssumption ↔ ∀ D : NUPPT, Negligible (G.dlinAdv D)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Subexponential symmetric DLIN has one positive security exponent before the adversary
[JLS26, §1.1, p. 3; Theorem 5.1, p. 21].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header: def SubexpDLIN : Prop := SubexpHard G.dlinAdv

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: Subexponential DLIN uses the shared `SubexpHard` predicate.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header: theorem subexpDLIN_iff : G.SubexpDLIN ↔ SubexpHard G.dlinAdv

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Sample the matrix form of DLIN in one symmetric source group
[GJLS21, Definition 3.3, p. 18]. The real vector is `A(r,s)` and the random vector is fully
uniform. Identifying the two source groups removes the duplicated bilateral copy.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
noncomputable def dlinMatrixSample (real : Bool) (κ : ℕ) : ProbComp (G.DLINChallenge κ) :=
  (publicParamsGen G κ).bind fun pp =>
  (ProbComp.sample (Fin 2 → ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order)).bind fun ab =>
  (ProbComp.sample (Fin 2 → ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order)).bind fun rs =>
  (ProbComp.sample (Fin 3 → ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order)).bind fun u =>
    .pure (G.dlinChallenge κ pp (pp.generator ^ (ab 0).val) (pp.generator ^ (ab 1).val)
      (pp.generator ^ (if real then ab 0 * rs 0 else u 0).val)
      (pp.generator ^ (if real then ab 1 * rs 1 else u 1).val)
      (pp.generator ^ (if real then rs 0 + rs 1 else u 2).val))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The matrix sampling law uses shared sequential public-parameter generation followed
by the displayed independent scalar draws.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinMatrixSample_eq (real : Bool) (κ : ℕ) :
    G.dlinMatrixSample real κ =
      (publicParamsGen G κ).bind fun pp =>
      (ProbComp.sample (Fin 2 → ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order)).bind fun ab =>
      (ProbComp.sample (Fin 2 → ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order)).bind fun rs =>
      (ProbComp.sample (Fin 3 → ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order)).bind fun u =>
        .pure (G.dlinChallenge κ pp (pp.generator ^ (ab 0).val) (pp.generator ^ (ab 1).val)
          (pp.generator ^ (if real then ab 0 * rs 0 else u 0).val)
          (pp.generator ^ (if real then ab 1 * rs 1 else u 1).val)
          (pp.generator ^ (if real then rs 0 + rs 1 else u 2).val))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Run the same distinguisher on the compressed symmetric matrix experiment
[GJLS21, Definition 3.3, p. 18]. The omitted matrix entries are zero and one, whose implicit
representations are determined by the public generator.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
noncomputable def dlinMatrixGame (D : NUPPT) (real : Bool) (κ : ℕ) : ProbComp Bool :=
  (G.dlinMatrixSample real κ).bind fun c =>
  (ProbComp.sample (D.Coins κ)).bind fun r =>
    .pure (D.distinguisherL κ (G.dlinEnc κ c) r)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The matrix experiment draws its typed challenge and independent distinguisher coins.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinMatrixGame_eq (D : NUPPT) (real : Bool) (κ : ℕ) :
    G.dlinMatrixGame D real κ =
      (G.dlinMatrixSample real κ).bind fun c =>
      (ProbComp.sample (D.Coins κ)).bind fun r =>
        .pure (D.distinguisherL κ (G.dlinEnc κ c) r)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The matrix DLIN advantage is the two-experiment advantage
[GJLS21, Definition 3.3, p. 18].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
noncomputable def dlinMatrixAdv (D : NUPPT) (κ : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  advantage (G.dlinMatrixGame D false κ) (G.dlinMatrixGame D true κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The matrix DLIN advantage uses the same advantage convention as canonical DLIN.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinMatrixAdv_eq (D : NUPPT) (κ : ℕ) :
    G.dlinMatrixAdv D κ =
      advantage (G.dlinMatrixGame D false κ) (G.dlinMatrixGame D true κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The probability that either of the two DLIN diagonal scalars is zero, averaged over the
public group draw. This is the explicit comparison slack between [JLS26, §1.1, p. 3] and
[GJLS21, Definition 3.3, p. 18]; it is needed because both sources allow zero scalars.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
noncomputable def dlinMatrixSlack (κ : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ProbComp.expect (ProbComp.sample (G.gen.Coins κ)) fun ρ =>
    2 / ((G.inst κ ρ).order : ℝ) - 1 / ((G.inst κ ρ).order : ℝ) ^ 2

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The diagonal-zero correction averages `2/p - 1/p^2` over the generated group.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinMatrixSlack_eq (κ : ℕ) :
    G.dlinMatrixSlack κ =
      ProbComp.expect (ProbComp.sample (G.gen.Coins κ)) fun ρ =>
        2 / ((G.inst κ ρ).order : ℝ) - 1 / ((G.inst κ ρ).order : ℝ) ^ 2

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The real tuple and compressed matrix presentations have identical acceptance laws
[GJLS21, Definition 3.3, p. 18; JLS26, §1.1, p. 3].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinMatrixGame_real_accept (D : NUPPT) (κ : ℕ) :
    accept (G.dlinMatrixGame D true κ) = accept (G.dlinGame D true κ)

theorem dlinMatrixGame_random_gap_le (D : NUPPT) (κ : ℕ) :
    |accept (G.dlinMatrixGame D false κ) - accept (G.dlinGame D false κ)| ≤
      G.dlinMatrixSlack κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Canonical DLIN bounds the matrix DLIN advantage with the explicit diagonal-zero slack
[GJLS21, Definition 3.3, p. 18; JLS26, §1.1, p. 3].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinMatrixAdv_le (D : NUPPT) (κ : ℕ) :
    G.dlinMatrixAdv D κ ≤ G.dlinAdv D κ + G.dlinMatrixSlack κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose:
Encode a source-group matrix row by row using the group's fixed-width point encoding.
This is serialization glue for the implicit matrices of [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
def groupMatrixEnc (M : Matrix (Fin rows) (Fin cols) B.G) : List Bool :=
  (List.ofFn fun i => (List.ofFn fun j => List.ofFn (B.encG (M i j))).flatten).flatten

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose: The group-matrix word concatenates the encoded entries, with rows and columns increasing.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem groupMatrixEnc_eq (M : Matrix (Fin rows) (Fin cols) B.G) :
    B.groupMatrixEnc M =
      (List.ofFn fun i => (List.ofFn fun j => List.ofFn (B.encG (M i j))).flatten).flatten

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose: A source-group matrix has one fixed-width block per entry. Serialization glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem length_groupMatrixEnc (M : Matrix (Fin rows) (Fin cols) B.G) :
    (B.groupMatrixEnc M).length = rows * cols * wG

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.prose: Group-matrix serialization is injective, including empty dimensions. Serialization glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGrou.header:
theorem groupMatrixEnc_injective :
    Function.Injective (B.groupMatrixEnc (rows := rows) (cols := cols))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
An MDDH challenge contains shared public parameters, the two-column base matrix and its
response matrix [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4, Assumption 1]. Private scalar witnesses are not stored.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
structure MDDHChallenge (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) where
  /-- The common public description and source-group generator. -/
  pp : PublicParams G κ
  /-- The implicit base matrix with exactly two columns. -/
  matrix : Matrix (Fin (ℓ.eval κ)) (Fin 2) (G.group κ pp.description.val).G
  /-- The implicit response with `d(κ)` columns. -/
  response : Matrix (Fin (ℓ.eval κ)) (Fin (d.eval κ)) (G.group κ pp.description.val).G

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Serialize the public parameters followed by the base and response matrices
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4, Assumption 1]. The encoding contains no group-generator coin strings.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
def mddhEnc (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (c : G.MDDHChallenge d ℓ κ) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode c.pp.encode
    (pairEncode ((G.group κ c.pp.description.val).groupMatrixEnc c.matrix)
      ((G.group κ c.pp.description.val).groupMatrixEnc c.response))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: A public matrix challenge serializes as its parameters, base matrix and response matrix.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhEnc_eq (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (c : G.MDDHChallenge d ℓ κ) :
    G.mddhEnc d ℓ κ c =
      pairEncode c.pp.encode
        (pairEncode ((G.group κ c.pp.description.val).groupMatrixEnc c.matrix)
          ((G.group κ c.pp.description.val).groupMatrixEnc c.response))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: Matrix-challenge encoding is injective on reachable public challenges. Serialization glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhEnc_injective (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (G.mddhEnc d ℓ κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The matrix-challenge word has a fixed polynomial length. Serialization glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem length_mddhEnc (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (c : G.MDDHChallenge d ℓ κ) :
    (G.mddhEnc d ℓ κ c).length =
      4 * G.descLen.eval κ + (2 + 4 * ℓ.eval κ + ℓ.eval κ * d.eval κ) * G.wG.eval κ + 8

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Sample a uniform two-column matrix `M`, an independent coefficient matrix `S`, and a
uniform response matrix `U`, after generating the public group parameters. Return `[M]`
with `[MS]` in the real branch and `[U]` in the random branch
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4, Assumption 1, with k=2].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
noncomputable def mddhSample (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (real : Bool) (κ : ℕ) :
    ProbComp (G.MDDHChallenge d ℓ κ) :=
  (publicParamsGen G κ).bind fun pp =>
  (ProbComp.sample (Matrix (Fin (ℓ.eval κ)) (Fin 2)
    (ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order))).bind fun M =>
  (ProbComp.sample (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin (d.eval κ))
    (ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order))).bind fun S =>
  (ProbComp.sample (Matrix (Fin (ℓ.eval κ)) (Fin (d.eval κ))
    (ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order))).bind fun U =>
    .pure ⟨pp, (G.group κ pp.description.val).expMat pp.generator M,
      (G.group κ pp.description.val).expMat pp.generator (if real then M * S else U)⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The MDDH sampling law is the displayed sequence of dependent public and uniform scalar
matrix draws.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhSample_eq (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (real : Bool) (κ : ℕ) :
    G.mddhSample d ℓ real κ =
      (publicParamsGen G κ).bind fun pp =>
      (ProbComp.sample (Matrix (Fin (ℓ.eval κ)) (Fin 2)
        (ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order))).bind fun M =>
      (ProbComp.sample (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin (d.eval κ))
        (ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order))).bind fun S =>
      (ProbComp.sample (Matrix (Fin (ℓ.eval κ)) (Fin (d.eval κ))
        (ZMod (G.group κ pp.description.val).order))).bind fun U =>
        .pure ⟨pp, (G.group κ pp.description.val).expMat pp.generator M,
          (G.group κ pp.description.val).expMat pp.generator (if real then M * S else U)⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Run a non-uniform PPT distinguisher on the encoded MDDH challenge with independent
machine coins [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4, Assumption 1].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
noncomputable def mddhGame (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (D : NUPPT) (real : Bool) (κ : ℕ) :
    ProbComp Bool :=
  (G.mddhSample d ℓ real κ).bind fun c =>
  (ProbComp.sample (D.Coins κ)).bind fun r =>
    .pure (D.distinguisherL κ (G.mddhEnc d ℓ κ c) r)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The MDDH game draws a challenge and independent distinguisher coins.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhGame_eq (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (D : NUPPT) (real : Bool) (κ : ℕ) :
    G.mddhGame d ℓ D real κ =
      (G.mddhSample d ℓ real κ).bind fun c =>
      (ProbComp.sample (D.Coins κ)).bind fun r =>
        .pure (D.distinguisherL κ (G.mddhEnc d ℓ κ c) r)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The uniform-matrix MDDH advantage is the absolute difference of acceptance probabilities
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4, Assumption 1].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
noncomputable def mddhAdv (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (D : NUPPT) (κ : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  advantage (G.mddhGame d ℓ D false κ) (G.mddhGame d ℓ D true κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: MDDH uses the library's two-experiment advantage.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhAdv_eq (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (D : NUPPT) (κ : ℕ) :
    G.mddhAdv d ℓ D κ =
      advantage (G.mddhGame d ℓ D false κ) (G.mddhGame d ℓ D true κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
With at most two rows the matrix assumption is statistical, with the explicit
rank-deficiency bound averaged over the public group draw
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4, paragraph after Assumption 1].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhAdv_smallRows_le (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (D : NUPPT)
    (hℓ : ∀ κ, ℓ.eval κ ≤ 2) (κ : ℕ) :
    G.mddhAdv d ℓ D κ ≤
      ProbComp.expect (ProbComp.sample (G.gen.Coins κ))
        (fun r => 2 / ((G.inst κ r).order : ℝ))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.GroupDescrip.prose:
A group description is reachable when the bilinear generator outputs it on some coin
string. Technical glue: the witness is a proposition, so it does not distinguish equal
descriptions or supply advice to an algorithm.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.GroupDescrip.header:
abbrev GroupDescription (G : BilinearGen) (κ : ℕ) : Type :=
  {d : List Bool // ∃ r : G.gen.Coins κ, G.desc κ r = d}

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupDescrip.prose: The description type consists of strings in the image of the bilinear generator.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.groupDescrip.header:
theorem groupDescription_eq (G : BilinearGen) (κ : ℕ) :
    GroupDescription G κ = {d : List Bool // ∃ r : G.gen.Coins κ, G.desc κ r = d}

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.PublicParams.prose:
Public parameters contain a reachable group description and a nonidentity generator
[GJLS21, Definition 4.1; Wee20, Section 2.1]. The generator is sampled uniformly from the
nonidentity source-group elements, separately after drawing the group description.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.PublicParams.header:
structure PublicParams (G : BilinearGen) (κ : ℕ) where
  /-- A description output by the group generator. -/
  description : GroupDescription G κ
  /-- The source-group generator used throughout this setup. -/
  generator : (G.group κ description.val).G
  /-- In a prime-order group every nonidentity element is a generator. -/
  generator_ne_one : generator ≠ 1

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.PublicParams.prose: The group carried by public parameters is the group described by their public word.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.PublicParams.header:
abbrev group {G : BilinearGen} {κ : ℕ} (pp : PublicParams G κ) :
    BilinearGroup (G.wG.eval κ) (G.wT.eval κ) := G.group κ pp.description.val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.PublicParams.prose: Reading the public group returns the generator's interpretation of the description.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.PublicParams.header:
theorem group_eq {G : BilinearGen} {κ : ℕ} (pp : PublicParams G κ) :
    pp.group = G.group κ pp.description.val

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.PublicParams.prose:
The positive modulus of public parameters is read from their group order. Honest
algorithms use this value, without computing an external prime schedule.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.PublicParams.header:
abbrev orderParam {G : BilinearGen} {κ : ℕ} (pp : PublicParams G κ) : ℕ+ :=
  ⟨pp.group.order, pp.group.order_prime.pos⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.PublicParams.prose: The positive public modulus has the same natural value as the public group's order.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.PublicParams.header:
theorem orderParam_val {G : BilinearGen} {κ : ℕ} (pp : PublicParams G κ) :
    (pp.orderParam : ℕ) = (G.group κ pp.description.val).order

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.PublicParams.prose:
Encode public parameters as the pair of the description and generator encoding.
This is the wire representation of the public parameters [GJLS21, Definition 4.1].
The public-parameter word pairs the group description and encoded generator.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.PublicParams.header:
theorem encode_eq {G : BilinearGen} {κ : ℕ} (pp : PublicParams G κ) :
    pp.encode = pairEncode pp.description.val
      (List.ofFn ((G.group κ pp.description.val).encG pp.generator))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.GeneratorDra.prose:
A nonidentity group element is the additional draw made after the group description
[Wee20, Section 2.1]. This is one draw type; no product sampler is constructed.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.GeneratorDra.header:
abbrev GeneratorDraw (G : BilinearGen) (κ : ℕ) (d : GroupDescription G κ) : Type :=
  {g : (G.group κ d.val).G // g ≠ 1}

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.generatorDra.prose: The generator draw is the subtype of nonidentity source-group elements.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.generatorDra.header:
theorem generatorDraw_eq (G : BilinearGen) (κ : ℕ) (d : GroupDescription G κ) :
    GeneratorDraw G κ d = {g : (G.group κ d.val).G // g ≠ 1}

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.publicParams.prose:
Attach a sampled generator to its public group description. This is the deterministic
core of the second stage of public-parameter generation [GJLS21, Definition 4.1].
The public-parameter core attaches the nonidentity generator without changing it.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.publicParams.header:
theorem publicParamsCore_eq (G : BilinearGen) (κ : ℕ) (d : GroupDescription G κ)
    (g : GeneratorDraw G κ d) : publicParamsCore G κ d g = ⟨d, g.val, g.property⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.publicParams.prose:
Generate the group description, then sample a nonidentity generator in that group
[Wee20, Section 2.1]. The dependent draws are sequenced; no uniform law on a dependent
sum is substituted for their joint law.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.publicParams.header:
noncomputable def publicParamsGen (G : BilinearGen) (κ : ℕ) :
    ProbComp (PublicParams G κ) :=
  (ProbComp.sample (G.gen.Coins κ)).bind fun r =>
    let d : GroupDescription G κ := ⟨G.desc κ r, ⟨r, rfl⟩⟩
    publicParamsCore G κ d <$> ProbComp.sample (GeneratorDraw G κ d)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.publicParams.prose: Public-parameter generation is the displayed pair of sequential dependent draws.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.publicParams.header:
theorem publicParamsGen_eq (G : BilinearGen) (κ : ℕ) :
    publicParamsGen G κ =
      (ProbComp.sample (G.gen.Coins κ)).bind fun r =>
        let d : GroupDescription G κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.order_eq_of_.prose:
A fixed order schedule agrees with the order of every reachable public parameter.
This is transport glue from the generated-instance reader, not an algorithm computing the
schedule or modulus.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.order_eq_of_.header:
theorem order_eq_of_publicParams (G : BilinearGen) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (κ : ℕ) (pp : PublicParams G κ) :
    (G.group κ pp.description.val).order = p κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.orderSchedul.prose:
A fixed order schedule of a prime-order group generator is prime at each parameter.
This proof reads one generated instance; honest algorithms do not evaluate the schedule.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.orderSchedul.header:
theorem orderSchedule_prime (G : BilinearGen) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (κ : ℕ) : (p κ).Prime

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.orderSchedul.prose: A fixed prime order schedule is nonzero, so its residue types are finite.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.orderSchedul.header:
theorem orderSchedule_neZero (G : BilinearGen) (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (κ : ℕ) : NeZero (p κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Advice fixes a hybrid-column index, a left randomizer, coefficient masks for the other
real columns, and uniform scalars for the other random columns. This is reduction glue for
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4]. The extra index value is a sentinel, ensuring inhabitation when `d=0`.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
abbrev MddhAdvice (p : ℕ → ℕ) (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) : Type :=
  Fin (d.eval κ + 1) ×
    Matrix (Fin (ℓ.eval κ)) (Fin 3) (ZMod (p κ)) ×
    Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin (d.eval κ)) (ZMod (p κ)) ×
    Matrix (Fin (ℓ.eval κ)) (Fin (d.eval κ)) (ZMod (p κ))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: Advice is exactly the hybrid index and its three known scalar matrices.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhAdvice_eq (p : ℕ → ℕ) (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) :
    MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ =
      (Fin (d.eval κ + 1) ×
        Matrix (Fin (ℓ.eval κ)) (Fin 3) (ZMod (p κ)) ×
        Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin (d.eval κ)) (ZMod (p κ)) ×
        Matrix (Fin (ℓ.eval κ)) (Fin (d.eval κ)) (ZMod (p κ)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Zero matrices and the first index give advice even when the response has no columns.
This is technical inhabitation glue, not a sampling algorithm.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
def mddhAdviceDefault (p : ℕ → ℕ) (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) : MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ :=
  ⟨0, 0, 0, 0⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The default advice consists of the first index and three zero matrices.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhAdviceDefault_eq (p : ℕ → ℕ) (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) :
    mddhAdviceDefault p d ℓ κ = ⟨0, 0, 0, 0⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: Advice is nonempty at every parameter, including `d(κ)=0`. Technical glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhAdvice_nonempty (p : ℕ → ℕ) (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) :
    Nonempty (MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
A fixed prime order schedule makes every advice type finite. Technical glue; no
additional nonzero-schedule assumption is imposed.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhAdvice_finite (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) :
    Finite (MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The advice word stores unary `κ`, shortest binary dimension headers, a one-hot hybrid
index, and fixed-width modular matrices. Scalars are advice, never drawn by the reduction.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
def mddhAdviceEnc (p : ℕ → ℕ) (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ)
    (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (ω : MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ) : List Bool :=
  letI : NeZero (p κ) := orderSchedule_neZero G p hp κ
  pairEncode (List.replicate κ true)
    (pairEncode (Candidates.natToList (Nat.size (d.eval κ)) (d.eval κ))
      (pairEncode (Candidates.natToList (Nat.size (ℓ.eval κ)) (ℓ.eval κ))
        ((List.ofFn fun i : Fin (d.eval κ + 1) => decide (i = ω.1)) ++
          Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (G.wG.eval κ) ω.2.1 ++
          Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (G.wG.eval κ) ω.2.2.1 ++
          Encoding.Modular.encodeMatrix (G.wG.eval κ) ω.2.2.2)))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The advice encoding exposes the security parameter, numeric dimensions and scalar blocks.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhAdviceEnc_eq (p : ℕ → ℕ) (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ)
    (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (ω : MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ) :
    G.mddhAdviceEnc p hp d ℓ κ ω =
      letI : NeZero (p κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
A polynomial bounds the parameter, dimension and one-hot headers and scalar blocks.
This is reduction-encoding glue. Binary lengths are bounded by their values plus one.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
def mddhAdviceLen (d ℓ : PolyExpr) : PolyExpr :=
  ((((PolyExpr.var.mul (PolyExpr.const 2)).add ((PolyExpr.const 2).mul d)).add ((PolyExpr.const
    2).mul ℓ)).add
    (PolyExpr.const 10)).add ((d.add (PolyExpr.const 1)).add
      ((((ℓ.mul (PolyExpr.const 3)).add ((PolyExpr.const 2).mul d)).add (ℓ.mul d)).mul G.wG))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The advice-length expression has one term for each serialized block.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhAdviceLen_eq (d ℓ : PolyExpr) :
    G.mddhAdviceLen d ℓ =
      ((((PolyExpr.var.mul (PolyExpr.const 2)).add ((PolyExpr.const 2).mul d)).add ((PolyExpr.const
        2).mul ℓ)).add
        (PolyExpr.const 10)).add ((d.add (PolyExpr.const 1)).add
          ((((ℓ.mul (PolyExpr.const 3)).add ((PolyExpr.const 2).mul d)).add (ℓ.mul d)).mul G.wG))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: Every advice family has the same polynomial length bound. Technical glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem length_mddhAdviceEnc_le (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (d ℓ : PolyExpr)
    (κ : ℕ) (ω : MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ) :
    (G.mddhAdviceEnc p hp d ℓ κ ω).length ≤ (G.mddhAdviceLen d ℓ).eval κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The advice word is injective on its index and scalar matrices. Technical glue.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhAdviceEnc_injective (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (G.mddhAdviceEnc p hp d ℓ κ)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The L1 typed preprocessor embeds the canonical DLIN column into a matrix hybrid. Its
role is to provide one challenge column and compute all other columns from fixed advice.
The per-column statistical correction is at most `4/p`; the hybrid contributes `d(κ)`.
All group entries are formed by products and known scalar powers [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
def mddhPreChallenge (p : ℕ → ℕ) (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ)
    (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (ω : MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ) (c : G.DLINChallenge κ) :
    G.MDDHChallenge d ℓ κ :=
  let castScalar := ZMod.ringEquivCongr (order_eq_of_publicParams G p hp κ c.pp).symm
  let L := fun i j => castScalar (ω.2.1 i j)
  let S := fun i j => castScalar (ω.2.2.1 i j)
  let U := fun i j => castScalar (ω.2.2.2 i j)
  let M := fun (i : Fin (ℓ.eval κ)) (j : Fin 2) =>
    if j = 0 then c.baseA ^ (L i 0).val * c.pp.generator ^ (L i 2).val
    else c.baseB ^ (L i 1).val * c.pp.generator ^ (L i 2).val
  let v := fun i =>
    c.responseA ^ (L i 0).val * c.responseB ^ (L i 1).val * c.responseSum ^ (L i 2).val
  ⟨c.pp, M, fun i j =>
    if j.val = ω.1.val then v i
    else if j.val < ω.1.val then M i 0 ^ (S 0 j).val * M i 1 ^ (S 1 j).val
    else c.pp.generator ^ (U i j).val⟩

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The typed preprocessor is precisely the displayed group-arithmetic embedding.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhPreChallenge_eq (p : ℕ → ℕ) (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ)
    (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (ω : MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ) (c : G.DLINChallenge κ) :
    G.mddhPreChallenge p hp d ℓ κ ω c =
      let castScalar

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The L1 string preprocessor serializes its typed matrix hybrid. Its input is a canonical
DLIN challenge and fixed advice; its output is the MDDH distinguisher's public input.
It contributes the same per-column correction as `mddhPreChallenge` and never samples.
The string preprocessor is the encoding of its typed matrix hybrid.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhPre_eq (p : ℕ → ℕ) (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ)
    (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) (ω : MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ) (c : G.DLINChallenge κ) :
    G.mddhPre p hp d ℓ κ ω c =
      G.mddhEnc d ℓ κ (G.mddhPreChallenge p hp d ℓ κ ω c)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The L1 DLIN reduction activates `D` once on the preprocessed matrix hybrid, using the
input coins truncated to `D.coinLen κ`. It never samples. Its comparison has a hybrid
factor `d(κ)` and total statistical correction `4d(κ)/p(κ)` [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
def dlinToMddh (p : ℕ → ℕ) (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ)
    (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (D : NUPPT) (ω : ∀ κ, MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ)
    (κ : ℕ) (c : G.DLINChallenge κ) (r : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  D.runAtL κ (G.mddhPre p hp d ℓ κ (ω κ) c) (r.take (D.coinLen κ))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The reduction runs the MDDH distinguisher on its deterministic preprocessed input.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem dlinToMddh_eq (p : ℕ → ℕ) (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ)
    (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (D : NUPPT) (ω : ∀ κ, MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ)
    (κ : ℕ) (c : G.DLINChallenge κ) (r : List Bool) :
    G.dlinToMddh p hp d ℓ D ω κ c r =
      D.runAtL κ (G.mddhPre p hp d ℓ κ (ω κ) c) (r.take (D.coinLen κ))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The full column-hybrid correction is `4d(κ)/p(κ)`. On a real DLIN challenge the base
matrix has rank below two with probability `p⁻²`. On a random challenge the augmented
matrix is singular with probability `3/p-3/p²+1/p³`. Their sum is at most `4/p` per column.
This is an explicit loss for the column-hybrid route to [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
noncomputable def mddhSlack (p : ℕ → ℕ) (d : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (d.eval κ : ℝ) * (4 / (p κ : ℝ))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose: The correction is the response-column count times the per-column `4/p` bound.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhSlack_eq (p : ℕ → ℕ) (d : PolyExpr) (κ : ℕ) :
    mddhSlack p d κ = (d.eval κ : ℝ) * (4 / (p κ : ℝ))

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
For every MDDH distinguisher, one advice family makes the column-hybrid bound hold for
EVERY machine realising the reduction, simultaneously at all parameters
[Wee20, §2.1, p. 4, polynomial-loss implementation of its cited implication].
The shared realisation predicate constrains only encoded challenges and coin strings of
the stated layout length, which suffices for this bound.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhAdv_le (p : ℕ → ℕ) (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ)
    (d ℓ : PolyExpr) (D : NUPPT) :
    ∃ ω : ∀ κ, MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ, ∀ B : NUPPT,
      B.RealizesOn G.dlinEnc D.coins (G.dlinToMddh p hp d ℓ D ω) →
      ∀ κ, G.mddhAdv d ℓ D κ ≤
        (d.eval κ : ℝ) * G.dlinAdv B κ + mddhSlack p d κ

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Realisability asks for one DLIN machine per fixed-advice reduction of a machine MDDH
adversary. This is the later machine-construction obligation, not an honest-algorithm
notion. The shared predicate constrains encoded challenges and layout-length coins only.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
def MDDHRealizable (p : ℕ → ℕ) (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ)
    (d ℓ : PolyExpr) : Prop :=
  ∀ (D : NUPPT) (ω : ∀ κ, MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ), ∃ B : NUPPT,
    B.RealizesOn G.dlinEnc D.coins (G.dlinToMddh p hp d ℓ D ω)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Matrix reduction realisability is exactly existence of a realiser for every machine and
advice family.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhRealizable_iff (p : ℕ → ℕ) (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ)
    (d ℓ : PolyExpr) :
    G.MDDHRealizable p hp d ℓ ↔
      ∀ (D : NUPPT) (ω : ∀ κ, MddhAdvice p d ℓ κ), ∃ B : NUPPT,
        B.RealizesOn G.dlinEnc D.coins (G.dlinToMddh p hp d ℓ D ω)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
The polynomial-over-order correction is subexponentially small at every exponent below
one when the prime schedule is at least `2^κ`. This uses the shared subexponential notion.
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhSlack_subexpSmall (p : ℕ → ℕ) (d : PolyExpr)
    (hpb : ∀ κ, 2 ^ κ ≤ p κ) {c : ℝ} (hc₀ : 0 < c) (hc₁ : c < 1) :
    SubexpSmall c (mddhSlack p d)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
DLIN hardness implies uniform-matrix MDDH negligibility once the fixed-advice reduction
functions have machine realisers [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddhAdv_negligible (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (d ℓ : PolyExpr)
    (hpb : ∀ κ, 2 ^ κ ≤ p κ) (hR : G.MDDHRealizable p hp d ℓ)
    (h : G.DLINAssumption) (D : NUPPT) : Negligible (G.mddhAdv d ℓ D)

TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..prose:
Subexponential DLIN implies subexponential MDDH for every fixed polynomial dimension
pair, under reduction realisability [Wee20, §2.1, p. 4; JLS26, §1.1, p. 3].
TCSlib.Cryptography.Pairing.BilinearGen..header:
theorem mddh_subexpHard (p : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ κ r, (G.inst κ r).order = p κ) (d ℓ : PolyExpr)
    (hpb : ∀ κ, 2 ^ κ ≤ p κ) (hR : G.MDDHRealizable p hp d ℓ)
    (h : G.SubexpDLIN) : SubexpHard (G.mddhAdv d ℓ)
